english.nesnd_jingyin_departure_title: The Prince of Huai Takes the Throne
english.nesnd_jingyin_departure_desc: News of the accession has reached [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName]. #bold [SCOPE.sCharacter('nesnd_jingyin_claimant').GetFullName]#! has received the ministers’ support and left for [SCOPE.sCountry('new_jingyin_owner').GetCapital.GetName] to take charge of government. Officials at the former residence must complete the handover, while those accompanying the new ruler will serve at the new court.
english.nesnd_external_hus_title: A Letter from Across the Sea
english.nesnd_external_hus_desc: News of the Southern succession has reached Dongzhou. The Zheng maritime empire that we fought for independence is again divided over who should rule it. Its opponents may seek support from our republic, while merchants watch for changes to the ports and routes on which they depend.\n\nWe can pursue those openings, but assistance abroad will draw on our own treasury and industry. The government must decide which relationships serve the republic and which commitments it can sustain.
english.nesnd_external_fra_desc: Southern envoys seek recognition and the continuation of old agreements, while India remains divided by disputes over the southern coast. French merchants, creditors and officers have interests in both regions. The government must decide whom to support and how far its money and arms should follow its diplomacy.
english.nesnd_external_qe1_desc: Caravans from Sichuan have brought news of the Southern dispute. Since the defeat at Dunhuang, Western Qin has had to consider its military strength and finances carefully. Renewed war in the east would make the roads through Bashu more important to trade and security alike. We should decide whether to cultivate Sichuan, support the anti-Wu coalition, or keep our resources at home.
english.nesnd_external_sha_desc: News of the Southern succession has reached the northern republic. Exiles recognise familiar names among those now disputing power, and some are already seeking contacts in Dongzhou. A friendly republic might supply funds or arms, but our government must decide what help it needs and what relationship it can sustain.
english.nesnd_external_bur_title: The River Mouth and the Court
english.nesnd_external_bur_desc: The Southern succession may alter the court’s dealings with a powerful neighbour. Trade along the rivers and the obligations inherited from existing treaties remain immediate concerns. Before committing money or arms to either side, we must consider our own status and which government can best protect our interests.
english.nesnd_external_mug_desc: The Southern succession offers another opening to raise our claims on the Indian coast. Ming possessions in Mysore and the arrangements of coastal traders remain sources of contention. Our ministers may seek French assistance in money or arms; if Southern rule still holds land in Mysore, we can also press our territorial claim.
english.nesnd_external_gbr_desc: The old alliance between France and Ming placed heavy pressure on British trade routes. A disputed succession in the Southern realm may create openings for commerce and diplomacy. Merchants seek access to its ports, while the government weighs the expense of supporting a foreign partner.
english.nesnd_external_rus_desc: Russia’s long eastern frontier gives the Southern dispute consequences far beyond its place of origin. A reliable trading partner or a government willing to accept our support might strengthen our position. We may wait for the outcome, or commit funds and arms while the rivals still need foreign friends.
english.nesnd_external_policy_reason: The Southern succession has placed old treaties, trade routes and overseas dependencies in question. Our government must choose which relationships to cultivate and whether to offer assistance or seek it from abroad. Existing agreements continue to bind their parties while new proposals are negotiated.
english.nesnd_external_follow: Prepare our response and make further enquiries.
english.nesnd_external_decline: Attend to our own affairs first.
english.nesnd_external_choose_desc: Choose a diplomatic partner. Existing treaties remain in force. Only one aid agreement can be concluded through this crisis.
english.nesnd_external_choose_opposition_desc: An anti-Wu coalition leader must exist. Our country must be independent and at peace with that government. Funds or arms require a separate proposal.
english.nesnd_external_offer_money_desc: Offer a transfer of @money!#v 500#! per week, binding for #v 1 year#!. This requires #v 26,000#! in reserves, fixed net income of at least #v 5,000#!, total net income of at least #v 1,000#! and eligibility to sign the treaty. The other government may refuse. The transfer continues after the binding period until withdrawn or renegotiated.
english.nesnd_external_offer_arms_desc: Offer a transfer of #v 10#! small arms, binding for #v 1 year#!. Our supply, prices, export allowance and transport must permit it. The other government may refuse; shortages or transport difficulties can suspend deliveries.
english.nesnd_external_request_tt: Our envoy will present the request in #v 7 days#!. No funds or goods are transferred before acceptance.
english.nesnd_external_status_choose: Select a partner, then consider the available terms.
english.nesnd_external_status_selected: Partner: #bold [ROOT.Var('nesnd_external_target').GetCountry.GetName]#!. The proposed funds and arms are shown in the relevant offers.
english.nesnd_external_status_pending: Our envoy awaits a reply. An unsigned request may still be withdrawn.
english.nesnd_external_status_committed: The treaty has been signed. Its fulfilment, suspension and withdrawal terms are available in the treaty interface.
english.nesnd_external_money_desc: The envoy from [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] offers @money!#v 500#! each week under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. Acceptance would establish the transfer between our treasuries.
english.nesnd_external_arms_desc: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] offers a transfer of #v 10#! small arms under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. Its envoy has presented the terms for our government to accept or refuse.
english.nesnd_external_commitment_tt: The treaty takes effect immediately. Its #bold binding period is not an expiry date#!. Early withdrawal carries the treaty’s penalties; normal withdrawal, suspension and costs can be reviewed in the treaty interface.
english.nesnd_external_request_money_desc: Ask the selected partner for @money!#v 500#! each week under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. The partner must be able and willing to pay.
english.nesnd_external_request_arms_desc: Request a transfer of #v 10#! small arms from the selected partner, binding for #v 1 year#!. Market access, transport and treaty eligibility must permit it. The partner may refuse.
english.nesnd_external_request_money_event_desc: The envoy from [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] requests financial assistance of @money!#v 500#! each week under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!.
english.nesnd_external_request_arms_event_desc: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] requests a transfer of #v 10#! small arms under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. Its envoy awaits our decision on the proposed deliveries.
english.nesnd_external_reconsider_desc: Choose another partner before an aid agreement is signed.
english.nesnd_external_mysore_desc: Assert a claim on Mysore while the Southern government still holds land there. Relations with it fall by #v 10#!. This establishes a claim without transferring territory or starting a war.
english.nesnd_external_mysore_tt: The Mysore claim enters our diplomatic agenda. Subject status and the right to wage war remain governed by existing relationships and treaties.
english.nesnd_external_cancel_request_desc: Withdraw the unsigned request. Existing treaties remain in force.
english.nesnd_external_dismiss_desc: Close the diplomatic mission and withdraw pending requests. Treaties already in force must be handled separately through diplomacy.
english.nesnd_external_resume_desc: Resume negotiations while the Southern crisis remains unresolved. An aid agreement already concluded cannot be repeated through this mission.
english.nesnd_external_end_desc: The Southern succession has reached a settlement. Our envoys have completed their mission, but treaties already signed remain in force. The government must continue meeting those obligations and attend to the relationships that survive the crisis.
english.nesnd_external_end_option: Close the mission and fulfil our agreements.
english.nesnd_phi_service_recovery_reason: The soldiers who sailed south with Lin Zexu brought the voices of Huguang to Luzon’s garrisons. Their pay, provisions and training now depend on the islands, while the administration must also keep ships ready for imperial service.\n\nThe cost of these obligations has become a question for both governments. Luzon seeks a new settlement of garrison expenses, naval service and tribute, so that its revenues can support the troops as well as the people who sustain them.
english.nesnd_phi_status_external: The subject relationship, shared market or peace between the two countries has changed. Payments under the agreement will cease. A new settlement must reflect our present income and obligations.
english.nesnd_phi_status_stalled: The paying country is unable to meet its obligations. The treaty may be suspended or the country in [concept_default]. Promised payments count as income only when received.
english.nesnd_phi_status_pending: Both governments must approve the proposal within 120 days. Until then, no money or ships change hands.
english.nesnd_phi_status_active: The agreement is in force. The subsidy ends 12 months after signature; garrison strength, naval staffing and local livelihoods must remain sustainable.
english.nesnd_phi_status_review: The subsidy has ended. Sustain the required finances, forces and livelihoods for three months. Renewed payments require the consent of both governments.
english.nesnd_phi_status_proposal: Request central funding for the garrison, or negotiate a division of naval responsibilities.
english.nesnd_phi_service_bar_detail:
Weekly balance excluding construction: #v £[Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_phi_budget').GetValue|0]#!
Crew required for a fully staffed fleet: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_phi_needed_crew').GetValue|0]#!
Unemployed workforce: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_phi_unemployment').GetValue|%1]#!
Workforce below the starvation threshold: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_phi_starving').GetValue|%1]#!

Each requirement fills one segment: a nonnegative balance excluding construction, no [concept_default] or [concept_bankruptcy], and any agreed subsidy actually being paid; at least #v 35 battalions#! in the standing army; at least #v 40 ships#! under the garrison agreement or #v 20 ships#! under the naval division, with #v 75%#! of crews and at least #v 80%#! naval maintenance fulfillment; unemployment at most #v 12%#! and no more than #v 15%#! of the workforce below the starvation threshold. Updated monthly.
english.nesnd_phi_continuity_bar_detail: Gain #p 1#! each month at peace with all four requirements met. A failure resets the count. The count also resets when the subsidy ends; three successful months after that are required to complete the Journal Entry.
english.nesnd_phi_request_a_button_desc: Use the confirmed commitment to Ming or Wu, which must match both governments’ present allegiances, to seek central funding for the overseas garrison. The central government must approve the expense before Luzon gives final consent.\n\n$nesnd_phi_route_1_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_request_b_button_desc: Propose a division between the ocean-going fleet and the defence of the islands, retaining the Western Administration’s garrison in Luzon. The agreement does not change either government’s political allegiance.\n\n$nesnd_phi_route_2_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_cancel_request_button_desc: Withdraw the unsigned proposal. Another may be submitted after 30 days. Existing diplomatic agreements remain in force.
english.nesnd_phi_withdraw_button_desc: Withdraw from the subsidy treaty negotiated here. Leaving during its binding period incurs the treaty’s Infamy and relations penalties. Tribute reductions, exemption from military service and other treaties retain their own terms. Ships already transferred remain with the central government.
english.nesnd_phi_route_1_terms_tt: The central government pays Luzon #v £8,000#! a week for #v 12 months#!. A separate treaty reduces the share of income paid in tribute by #v 10 percentage points#!. Luzon retains its fleet and garrison. The central government needs at least #v £10,000#! in weekly surplus excluding construction, #v £100,000#! in reserves, and eligibility for both treaties. The subsidy treaty is withdrawn at the end of the year; the tribute reduction retains its own terms.
english.nesnd_phi_route_2_terms_tt: On the first agreement, Luzon transfers #v 20 ships of the line#! that it owns and that are not engaged in war. It retains #v 20 frigates#! and the garrison. The central government pays #v £3,000#! weekly for #v 12 months#!, and concludes separate treaties for reduced tribute and exemption from military service. It needs at least #v £5,000#! in weekly surplus excluding construction and #v £60,000#! in reserves. Renewals do not transfer more ships. The subsidy ends after a year; the other agreements retain their own terms.
english.nesnd_phi_usm_accept_tt: Return the approved terms to Luzon for final consent. Treaty eligibility, finances, the subject relationship and the fleet must still meet the requirements. No subsidy is paid and no ships are transferred yet.
english.nesnd_phi_reject_tt: Return the proposal. Another may be submitted after 90 days.
english.nesnd_phi_defer_tt: Do not sign this agreement. Negotiations may resume after 30 days.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.1.d: Luzon asks the central government to share the cost of the troops and ships maintained on the islands. Its administration argues that overseas service cannot depend indefinitely on local revenue alone.\n\nThe proposal provides #v £8,000#! a week for one year, alongside a reduction in tribute. It now falls to the central government to decide whether to undertake these obligations.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.1.a: Approve the funding and seek Luzon’s consent.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.2.d: Luzon proposes to transfer twenty ships of the line to the central navy. The frigates would remain to defend the islands, as would the garrison. Taking over the ships would also make the central government responsible for their crews, bases and supplies.\n\nIn return, Luzon seeks exemption from military service, reduced tribute and #v £3,000#! a week for one year to support the reorganization.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.2.a: Agree to this division of responsibilities.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.3.d: The central government has approved Luzon’s request. It offers #v £8,000#! a week for one year, with reduced tribute under a separate agreement. The fleet and garrison would remain Luzon’s responsibility.\n\nThe administration in Manila must now give its consent before the payments can begin.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.4.d: The central government has accepted the proposed division of naval duties. The frigates will defend the islands, and the Western Administration’s garrison will remain in Luzon.\n\nLuzon’s signature will confirm the ship transfer, reduced tribute and exemption from service, together with #v £3,000#! in weekly payments for one year. A renewal will retain the previous transfer without requiring further ships.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.4.a: Sign and carry out the transfer.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.5.d: Both governments have signed. The central treasury must now make the agreed payments, while Luzon’s administration must use its revenues to support the garrison, the fleet and the islands’ civilian needs.\n\nThe coming year will show whether these obligations can be maintained after the temporary subsidy ends.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.6.d: The year of payments is over, and the subsidy treaty has ended as agreed. Luzon must now support its remaining forces from current revenues or negotiate fresh assistance. Its other obligations remain governed by the existing subject relationship and treaties.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.7.d: The subsidy can no longer continue on the agreed terms. Luzon’s military and naval authorities must revise their spending. Any new agreement will have to reflect the present subject relationship, market arrangements and military obligations.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.8.d: For three months after the subsidy ended, Luzon has maintained its finances, forces and civilian livelihoods. The garrison remains supplied and the fleet has the crews it needs. The administration can plan its next season of spending from revenues it actually receives.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.10.d: The two governments have amended the treaty through diplomatic negotiations. Its terms now differ from the earlier military funding agreement. Luzon’s administration will follow the revised treaty; its payment schedule and other obligations can be reviewed in the diplomacy panel.
english.nesnd_phi_request_cash_a_button_desc: Agree on a weekly contribution from the central government towards the garrison and ocean-going fleet. A confirmed commitment to Ming or Wu must match both governments’ present allegiances.\n\n$nesnd_phi_cash_1_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_request_cash_b_button: Divide Naval Duties with Fixed Funding
english.nesnd_phi_request_cash_b_button_desc: Transfer the ships of the line to the central government, retaining frigates to defend the islands and the existing garrison. Negotiate fixed funding for the new arrangement. This agreement does not change allegiance to Ming or Wu, neutrality or independence.\n\n$nesnd_phi_cash_2_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_cash_1_terms_tt: The central government pays Luzon #v £8,700#! weekly for #v 12 months#!. Luzon retains its garrison and fleet. Tribute continues under the existing subject relationship; this agreement neither reduces the tribute rate nor changes Liberty Desire. The central government needs at least #v £10,000#! in weekly surplus excluding construction, #v £100,000#! in reserves, and eligibility for the subsidy treaty. Payments begin only after both governments consent and end after the agreed year.
english.nesnd_phi_cash_2_terms_tt: The first agreement transfers #v 20 ships of the line#! to the central government. Luzon retains #v 20 frigates#! and the garrison, and gains exemption from military service if eligible. The central government pays #v £3,700#! weekly for #v 12 months#!. Tribute continues at the existing rate. The central government needs at least #v £5,000#! in weekly surplus excluding construction and #v £60,000#! in reserves. Renewals do not transfer additional ships; the end of the year terminates only this subsidy.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.11.d: Luzon requests an annual contribution towards the troops and ships it maintains for imperial service. Tribute would continue under the existing arrangement, while the central treasury would take on a separate share of the military expense.\n\nThe proposed payment is #v £8,700#! a week for one year.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.11.a: Approve the subsidy and seek Luzon’s consent.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.12.d: The central government has approved #v £8,700#! in weekly payments for one year. Luzon would continue paying tribute under its present obligations and remain responsible for the fleet and garrison.\n\nThe administration in Manila must give final consent to begin the payments.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.13.d: Luzon asks the central navy to take over twenty ships of the line, retaining the frigates and garrison for local defence. The central government would provide their new bases, crews and supplies.\n\nTribute would continue on the existing terms. Luzon seeks #v £3,700#! a week for one year and exemption from further military service under the agreed arrangements.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.13.a: Approve the division and its funding.
english.nesnd_phi_finance.14.d: The central government has accepted the naval division. Twenty ships of the line would pass to its navy, while the frigates and garrison remain in Luzon. Renewals retain the transfer already made.\n\nThe agreement provides #v £3,700#! a week for one year. Tribute and exemption from military service follow their separate terms. Luzon must now give final consent.
english.nesnd_phi_propose_native_a_tt: Submit the proposal to the central government. If approved, it returns to Luzon for final consent. Proposed terms:\n\n$nesnd_phi_route_1_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_propose_native_b_tt: Submit the proposal to the central government. If approved, it returns to Luzon for final consent. Proposed terms:\n\n$nesnd_phi_route_2_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_propose_cash_a_tt: Submit the proposal to the central government. If approved, it returns to Luzon for final consent. Proposed terms:\n\n$nesnd_phi_cash_1_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_phi_propose_cash_b_tt: Submit the proposal to the central government. If approved, it returns to Luzon for final consent. Proposed terms:\n\n$nesnd_phi_cash_2_terms_tt$
english.nesnd_supply_preparations_reason: Wu shipping brings grain from the Southern Seas, distant timber and foreign goods into the Southern realm. Inland workshops, garrisons and academies already depend on those exchanges. Provincial powers differ, but production and livelihoods can scarcely stand apart from the common market. Closing a port or severing a trade route spreads losses far beyond it.\n\nAs the Ming court and Hangzhou dispute the succession, [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] must keep its government and forces functioning. Offices need paper, garrisons need recruits and arms, and academy students are preparing to enter political life. We must maintain trade with willing partners and make local workshops, schools and livelihoods capable of enduring the present disruption.
english.nesnd_supply_status_war: #n War has reached the trading routes.#! Requisitions and disrupted shipping have broken the previous period of stability.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_status_inputs: #n Workshops and garrisons lack reliable supplies.#! Paper, tools and arms are straining their budgets.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_status_jobs: #n Workshops and offices still lack workers.#! More posts must be filled to sustain their business.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_status_livelihood: #n Livelihoods remain insecure.#! Unemployment, grain prices and famine threaten commercial life.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_status_diplomacy: Commercial contacts remain undecided. Send envoys to discuss them, or leave merchants to maintain their own dealings.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_status_stable: #p Supplies, employment and livelihoods are becoming stable.#! Sustain them for a season to establish lasting trade.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_invite_desc: Send envoys to discuss commercial relations and improve diplomatic ties. Existing market exchange continues.
english.nesnd_supply_invitation_tt: The envoys arrive in seven days and serve for six months.
english.nesnd_supply_self_desc: Withdraw the special mission and pending requests, leaving merchants to continue their existing trade. Market membership and signed treaties remain unchanged.
english.nesnd_supply_end_contact_desc: Recall the mission and end these commercial contacts. Existing market exchange and signed treaties continue.
english.nesnd_supply_end_contact_tt: End these contacts. If this leaves commercial arrangements unresolved, consecutive stable weeks restart; signed treaties remain in force.
english.nesnd_supply_trade_desc: Give the two countries’ merchants reciprocal trading advantages through a treaty.
english.nesnd_supply_trade_request_tt: In #v 7 days#!, propose a reciprocal trade treaty binding for #v 2 years#!. The other government may accept or refuse.
english.nesnd_supply_finish_desc: After supplies, employment, livelihoods and commercial arrangements remain stable for #v 12 weeks#!, first completion grants #p +100#! [concept_influence] for #v 2 years#!.
english.nesnd_supply_dismiss_desc: Recall the mission and return to commercial arrangements later. Existing mission expenses remain due until their term ends.
english.nesnd_supply_resume_desc: Reconnect with merchants, secure supplies and employment, and restore dealings with other states.
english.nesnd_supply.1.d: Envoys from [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_supply_requester').GetName] have brought a request from their merchants. They hope to maintain procurement contacts between the two countries and exchange information about supplies of paper, timber and manufactured goods, preserving trading opportunities as the political situation changes.\n\nThese contacts would broaden our commercial relations, but need officials to receive the mission and merchants to sustain the exchanges. [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] may appoint representatives to hear the proposed arrangements.
english.nesnd_supply.1.b: Our domestic affairs must come first.
english.nesnd_supply.2.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_supply_requester').GetName] proposes a formal treaty granting reciprocal trade advantages. Merchants hope to expand their markets, while those buying supplies seek more stable commercial relations. Once signed, both countries will be obliged to fulfil its terms.
english.nesnd_supply.3.d: For the past season, workshops and garrisons in [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] have been able to buy what they need, while schools, offices and factories have filled their posts. Merchants have renewed their trading contacts, and people across the states have supported themselves through production and exchange.\n\nThe Southern political dispute continues. The cargo ships leaving our ports give us the means to keep trading through it.
english.nesnd_supply_invite_cne: Send Envoys to the Chinese Empire
english.nesnd_supply_hus_preparations_reason: Immigrants and merchant ships built the republic’s coastal towns. War against Wu brought its states together; the northern alliance opened further markets. Work in the harbours, production in the mills and provincial revenue now depend upon these connections.\n\nNews of the southern dispute crosses the ocean. Whether we continue in the shared market or arrange our own trade, production and livelihoods at home must endure.
english.nesnd_supply_finish_shared_desc: Continue trading in the existing common market. Maintain all conditions for #v 12 weeks#! to gain #p +100#! [concept_influence] for #v 2 years#! on first completion.
english.nesnd_supply_finish_autonomous_desc: Continue trading in the market our country already controls. Maintain all conditions for #v 12 weeks#! to gain #p +100#! [concept_influence] for #v 2 years#! on first completion.
english.nesnd_supply_status_bankruptcy: #n The treasury is bankrupt.#! Finances must recover before a new period of stability can be established.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
english.nesnd_supply_workforce_ready_tt: National workforce unemployment is at most #v 12%#!, and at most #v 20%#! in states with at least #v 50,000#! workers.
english.nesnd_supply_rules:
#bold Supplies#!
Paper, tools and small arms must have no local shortages and cost no more than #v 50%#! above base price; Dongzhou also requires hardwood.

#bold Buildings and workers#!
Each required building type must have at least one building staffed to #v 75%#! without input shortages. Huguang requires a university and barracks; Sichuan a tooling workshop and either an iron mine or logging camp; Guangxi a paper mill and logging camp; Dongzhou a port and government administration. If recruitment is difficult, check [concept_pop_qualifications], [concept_building_wage] and input supplies.

#bold Livelihoods#!
Unemployed workers may be at most #v 12%#! of the national workforce. States with at least #v 50,000#! workers have a limit of #v 20%#!. Subsistence workers count as employed. There must be no famine or local grain shortage, and grain must cost no more than #v 25%#! above base price.
Unemployed workforce: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_supply_unemployed').GetValue|0] / [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_supply_workforce').GetValue|0]#! (#v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_supply_unemployment').GetValue|%1]#!). States above the local unemployment limit: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_supply_critical_states').GetValue|0]#!.

#bold Stable commerce#!
A shared market automatically fulfils the commercial-arrangements requirement. A country alone in its market may choose a contact or leave dealings to its merchants. Maintain all four conditions for #v 12 weeks#!. War, bankruptcy, a change of market or failure of any condition restarts the consecutive count.
english.nesnd_tenasserim_recovery_reason: Dye shipments connect the southern plantations to the imperial market. Rent, advances and debt bind many village households to that trade. New paid work and viable smallholdings will determine whether the interior can sustain its own customers and savings.
english.nesnd_ten_status_sampling: Local officials are reporting on employment and livelihoods over the first three months. Logging commissions and legislation may proceed in the meantime.
english.nesnd_ten_status_war: War has interrupted the recovery. Ports, shipping and access to markets must be restored.
english.nesnd_ten_status_working_hungry: Many hungry workers already have jobs. Review household income, rent, taxation and food prices.
english.nesnd_ten_status_jobs: Unemployed workforce exceeds 12%. Check existing vacancies, wages and qualifications.
english.nesnd_ten_status_income: Employment has improved, but household livelihoods remain below the target.
english.nesnd_ten_status_review: Local livelihoods are recovering. At least one industry that does not use arable land must also reach 75% staffing.
english.nesnd_ten_conditions_bar_detail:
Unemployed workforce: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_unemployment').GetValue|%1]#!
Workforce below the starvation threshold: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_starving').GetValue|%1]#!
Employed and below the starvation threshold: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_working_hungry').GetValue|%1]#!
Workforce household [concept_sol]: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_sol').GetValue|1]#!
[concept_market_access]: #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_access').GetValue|%1]#!

Requirements: unemployment at most #v 12%#!; at most #v 25%#! below the starvation threshold and living standards of at least #v 6.5#!; market access of at least #v 85%#!; peace and no active [concept_bankruptcy] penalty. Shares are calculated from the workforce in our part of Tenasserim and updated monthly. Subsistence farmers count as employed.
english.nesnd_ten_continuity_bar_detail: After the first three months of local reports, gain #p 1#! per month with all four livelihood requirements met and at least one logging camp, fishery, iron mine, tooling workshop, textile mill or food industry #v 75%#! staffed without input shortages. A failure resets the consecutive-month count. Completion grants #p +10%#! qualifications gain locally for #v 24 months#!.\n\nNational institutional reform proceeds through $je_reform_indies$.
english.nesnd_ten_build_button_desc: Commission a logging camp to provide paid work without taking arable land.\n\nEach commission queues #v 1 level#! of government construction, up to #v 2 commissions#! at least #v 6 months#! apart. Any existing logging camp must be #v 75%#! staffed without input shortages. Wood must sell for at least #v 50%#! of its base price, the treasury must hold #v £5,000#!, and local capacity must permit construction. Normal construction and treasury costs apply. Simple forestry can be used where tools or trained machinists are scarce.
english.nesnd_ten_build_result_tt: Queue one logging-camp level in Tenasserim. Normal construction costs apply; completion and hiring occur through the economy.
english.nesnd_ten_train_button_desc: Pay 2.5% of weekly total income, minimum £1,000 (estimated £[Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_training_quote').GetValue|0]). Local qualifications +10% for 12 months; 12-month cooldown. Requires an existing nonfarm vacancy. Laws and household conditions still govern qualification eligibility.
english.nesnd_ten_tenant_button_desc: Replace serfs’ personal dependence with tenancy, allowing farmers to plan their livelihoods after paying rent.\n\nBegin enacting Tenant Farmers. The law must be enactable and supported by an interest group in government or a political movement with at least #v 10%#! support. Enactment chance must be at least #v 15%#! and legitimacy at least #v 25#!, with no other law being enacted, war or revolution.
english.nesnd_ten_abolish_button_desc: Abolish slavery so that workers can no longer be held as another person’s property.\n\nOnce serfdom has ended, local unemployment must be at most #v 15%#! and three months of local reports must be available. The support, enactment-chance and legitimacy requirements are the same as for Tenant Farmers. Emancipation takes effect when the law passes.
english.nesnd_ten_compromise_button_desc: During tenant or abolition enactment, pay 25% of weekly income, minimum £5,000 (estimated £[Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_ten_compromise_quote').GetValue|0]). Requires landowner clout of 20%. Landowner approval +3 for 24 months; 24-month cooldown. No change to law stance or enactment chance.
english.nesnd_ten_dismiss_button_desc: Return the programme’s duties to the existing administration and merchants, ending its special instruction. The programme can reopen after one year.
english.nesnd_ten_dismiss_tt: End the programme and withdraw its practical instruction. It may reopen after one year. Queued construction, ongoing legislation and compensation already paid remain in effect; previous commissions and rewards still count.
english.nesnd_ten_continue_tt: Continue the Tenasserim programme with its existing construction, legislation and funding arrangements.
english.nesnd_ten_reopen_desc: Resume efforts to improve employment and rural livelihoods in Tenasserim. Previous commissions still count towards the limit, and the period of recovery begins again.
english.nesnd_tenasserim.1.d: The Tenasserim programme has run into difficulty. Logging camps and workshops need employers able to pay wages; villagers need tenancy and credit arrangements that leave them a livelihood. The practical instruction provided by the authorities also requires sustained funding.\n\nThe government must decide whether to keep committing resources or return these responsibilities to the existing administration and merchants.
english.nesnd_tenasserim.2.d: Paid work is bringing money back to the villages of Tenasserim. Household purchases support the local market, and fewer residents have lost their livelihoods. Provincial authorities will continue practical instruction for two years as these new trades take root.
english.nesnd_japan_war_collapse_reason: Wu armies have crossed the sea. Kyoto sustains the court's authority, while Kanto holds the military strength of the great houses. If both fall, the Toyotomi can no longer command the domains. The victors will determine the boundaries and standing of the three successor governments.
english.nesnd_japan_war_collapse_status: While at war with Wu, hostile occupation of #bold both Kyoto and Kanto#! causes the shogunate to collapse. Either centre remaining free allows resistance to continue. An enforced Wu war demand also leads to the defeat settlement.
english.nesnd_japan_war_collapse_fallen: The shogunate has fallen. The Toyotomi, Tokugawa and imperial territories are being reorganised. Land still occupied by a third country awaits settlement of the fighting.
english.nesnd_xiangyang_camp_journal_reason: Xiangyang commands the Han River and the inland military roads. Its soldiers follow Chen Dongyang's reforms, opposing both the Zheng usurpation and a return to the old gentry's rule. Central supply and regular drills give this inland army the means to hold its ground.
english.nesnd_xiangyang_camp_desc: Coordinated arms and provisions sustain a disciplined defence of the Han River.
english.nesnd_capital_surrender_tt: This country will be annexed by Wu.
english.dyn_c_ussr_californias: United Socialist Council Republics of California
english.je_confederation_of_the_rhine_reason: From 1806 to 1828, under the design of Napoleon Bonaparte, many German states were unified under a single government - #bold Confederation of the Rhine#!. Under this system, Napoleon consolidated his control over the German states through proxies, suppressing the power of #bold Prussia#! and #bold Austria#!. However, with the Confederation's own economic problems, Napoleon's deteriorating health, and the soft reign of his son to other great powers, the Confederation's unity was lost. Many German states were granted independence, leaving opportunities for Prussia's customs union plans. \n\nBut the era of the King of Rome has long past! [SCOPE.sCountry('rhine_overlord').GetName] must reorganize the affairs of the Confederation to ensure that the German people do not grow into a threat to our continental hegemony.
english.je_confederation_of_the_rhine_confederat: With the collapse of the Prussian Alliance, we shall restore the united #bold Rhine Confederation#!, constraining the ambitions of German powers in the region.
english.formation.20.d: Opposing both Austrian and Prussian designs on their land, a confederation of German states has unified into a restored [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName]. The Confederation stands united to assert its sovereignty in the face of its enemies.
english.formation.20.f: Years after Napoleon's death, his influence might still be felt across Europe. This confederacy is but one of many projects from his plan for Europe. Perhaps it can be turned to a nobler purpose.
english.modifier_building_group_bg_subsistence_s: Bonus or penalty to [concept_sol] for subsistence farmers
english.modifier_building_group_bg_manufacturing: Bonus or penalty to input and output of subsistence agriculture
english.flavorCNE.1.d:
The ruling bloc of the Empire of China was born in the great revolutionary era barely twenty years ago. They witnessed the old military clans and their two empires ground into dust by that vast upheaval. On those ruins, new officer corps led by Mu Zhongtang rose in the people's name, cleared out corruption and radical terror. Then, he the great led the founding of our great empire upon the promise of 'equal land rights and people's governance'.

Everything should have remained so...

In 1819, after founding emperor Mu Zhongtang and his military meritorious allies completed 'the land purge' across all North China, the empire replaced the republic to public acclaim. Yet the celebrated reforms were far from complete. Landlords in Liaodong and the northwest escaped punishment due to close military ties. The collapse of war bonds after the failed southern campaign of 1820-22 pushed countless small households into poverty. At this moment of peril, the founding emperor decisively revived the slogan of 'land rights revolution'. Land reorganization profits and population mobility stabilized a faltering imperial economy. But as peace endured and reforms deepened, a dark current gathered in the shadows. Vested interests in the army, the tycoons, the officials, and even old gentry stripped of surplus lands began to return. Their schemes, resentment, and desire now corrode the foundations of the imperial ideals like some deadly acid...
english.flavorCNE.1.f: When a broad table is to be made, and the edges of planks do not fit, the artist takes a little from both, and makes a good joint.\n- Benjamin Franklin
english.flavorCNE.1.1: The people's interests build the empire; those unable to defend them perish, however strong.
english.ce_cne_land_reform_reason: This movement began with the Western Qin Great Revolution of 1810. People of the age understood it as a modern economic transformation arising among the agrarian states of the East, where powerful lineages had long dominated rural life. Through purchase or compulsory confiscation, land accumulated beyond all measure by its old owners was redistributed among a portion of the peasantry. The aim was to break the lineages’ hold over the rural population. The ruling group of the Empire of China suspended the movement during its rise to power. Around Mu Zhongtang’s southern campaign of 1820, however, he and his confidants revived it to restore the economy, free productive activity and mobilise peasants and soldiers.
english.owns_3_modern_china_provinces.ce.tt: You and your subjects #bold fully control#! at least three #bold Chinese provinces#! (for example, Shanxi Province)
english.ce_cne_land_draft_failing_reason: The imperial ruling bloc is centered on the Mu military-merit aristocracy and a new stratum of rising gentry around them. Their memory of the Western Qin Great Revolution that destroyed the Qin-Yan Empire in North China remains vivid, so they were once willing to concede to lower classes for self-preservation. Yet as time passes and internal struggles deepen, both reason and fear decay. They will inevitably turn against certain progressive policies...
english.ce_cne_land_draft_failing_goal: If #bold any one#! of the following conditions is true, progress increases by #bold 3#! per #bold year#!:\n$ig_landowners$ is [concept_powerful] or [concept_in_government]\n$ig_devout$ is [concept_powerful] or [concept_in_government]
english.cne_landreform_failure_tracker_100: When progress reaches #bold 100#!, the corruption journal is completed automatically
english.NOT_TRIGGER_MARKET_ACCESS_LESS_THAN: No [State.GetName] [concept_market_access] is less than or equal to #bold 85%#!
english.ce_cne_war_with_western_qin: Deal with the Western Qin Separatist Regime
english.ce_cne_reform_limited_market_access_reas: In the years of turbulence, wartime and social revolution created a special boom that encouraged wild local economic growth. This produced market instability and serious internal trade imbalances. It is time to reverse that trend.
english.ce_cne_war_with_western_qin_reason: The so-called 'Western Qin' regime entrenched in the Western Regions and Transoxiana occupies Huaxia land and people while continuously raiding and infiltrating our western provinces. Its existence gravely disrupts political and economic reform in the northwest. This hostile force must be destroyed or neutralized.
english.ce_cne_war_with_usm_reason: Southern pretenders were already imperial enemies in the era of founding emperor Mu Zhongtang. Military figures such as Zhu Banbo, Lin Zexu, Xiao Huli, and Lin Hanhan blocked our national army's southern unification drive, forcing temporary peace. Yet our state was founded upon unification as a national vision. So long as North and South remain divided, domestic unrest and suspicion will not cease.
english.ce_cne_technology_advantage_reason: After the failed southern campaign, many thinkers began reconsidering the meaning of our state's existence. Not only do former-regime remnants yearn for the Qin-Yan Empire, some even claim every founding institution is inferior to ancient models. In this age where republican dreams have dimmed, such reactionary currents still attract followers. To destroy this countercurrent, we must stride forward in the realm of thought.
english.ce_cne_reform_legal_system_reason: Founding emperor Mu Zhongtang carried the legacy of the Western Qin Revolution and opened the grand project of a national empire. To advance national development and civic welfare, first-generation chancellors Cha Wanfang and Zhang Baili set out the founding blueprint in Four Strategies for Building Great Unity. But this alone is not enough. To stabilize hearts, defeat poverty, and build an 'eternal empire of free will,' we must continually reform imperial politics itself - turn our efforts and ideas into law, and carve them into stone.
english.ce_cne_reform_limited_market_access_expl: No province in the country has [concept_market_access] below #bold 80%#!
english.qe1_is_mengyou_tt: Reconcile with Western Qin and form an alliance
english.usm_is_mengyou_tt: Reconcile with Southern Ming and form an alliance

english.ce_cne_war_with_usm_explain: While this journal is incomplete, #bold Imperial Corruption#! [concept_journal_entry] will #bold each year#! #bold gain 1 progress#!

english.flavorCNE.2.d: As time passes and politics shift, the imperial land-rights revolution launched by founder Mu Zhongtang can no longer be pushed forward. We must accept the present condition of domestic land ownership. All related policies and decrees will be reviewed in the coming months. Measures still useful to government and the economy will be retained; those that fail review must be abolished swiftly and decisively to prevent further instability.
english.flavorCNE.2.f: The people's interests build the empire; those unable to defend them perish, however strong.\n- Mu Zhongtang, Ten Admonitions to Ministers on the Haihe Inspection
english.flavorCNE.2.1: We admit failure and preserve the status quo.
english.flavorCNE.3.t: Victory of the Land Rights Revolution
english.flavorCNE.3.d:
Our revised laws on land, employment and family relations have reached every corner of the Empire and established a new economic order. We have freed people from the bonds of kinship that held them for thousands of years. The fields have returned to their proper place as a natural resource.

As the old lineages and their land can no longer bind the peasantry, young faces, dusty yet full of life, stream from the countryside into the cities. They dream of a new life built through human intelligence and science. The remnants of hereditary power disguise themselves as local associations and try to regain control over them. Police batons and the magistrate’s gavel will break their ambitions.

Once more we have brought the founding emperor Mu Zhongtang’s ideals into reality. We have shown that this Empire was built for the interests of the Huaxia nation. It will protect even the weakest person’s freedom to choose a future. Those now seeking happiness in the cities are bringing new prosperity to the Empire.
english.flavorCNE.3.f: From each according to ability, by free will. The state voices the people’s aspirations; together they build the Empire. \n—Cha Wanfang, Memorial on the People’s Grant of the Imperial Mandate
english.flavorCNE.3.1: Human power, expressed in changing fate, is the highest source of wealth.
english.CNE_land_draft_debuff: Land Rights Held by the Military Merit Bloc
english.tooltip_is_modern_china_state: Is an agrarian province in Northern Ming China
english.flavorCNE.4.t: The Petition of Ten Thousand People
english.flavorCNE.4.d: Land rights revolution is economic reform, but also a harsh political movement. It transfers wealth stolen for millennia by an old social order into the hands of a new elite born only decades ago. Such a process cannot end through monetary redemption alone. It inevitably involves legal pursuit, fraud, repeated contestation, betrayal by executors, and even brutal violence.\n\nThis process enrages local gentry and frightens socially undecided middle strata. The latter are easily rallied by the former and turned into their vanguard.
english.flavorCNE.4.f: Heavenly slaughter leaves no escape; earth's sweep gives no refuge. At year's end, with only tiny savings left, how can officials bear to take them?
english.flavorCNE.4.2: The tide is fierce; we should avoid its edge for now.
english.flavorCNE.5.d: Soldiers have lives and families. Many are younger sons of clans once expected to rise; some are destitute men cast out by those clans, hoping army life can change their fate. The latter have been overzealous in the movement, while the former often became obstacles.\n\nRecently we received reports that grassroots officers colluded with local gentry. Most had received letters from home saying their clans' lands were declared illegal or forcibly redeemed by government. They organized and acted with military discipline and efficiency. Local politics turned unstable and the impact was severe.
english.flavorCNE.5.2: What can they do, overturn heaven itself?
english.flavorCNE.6.d: Land commissioners in [SCOPE.sState('cne_land_reform_mess_imprisonment_state').GetName] have arrested villagers who drafted petitions over disputed titles and placed them in military custody for concealing property. Officers widened the arrests to local gentry, teachers and clerks who kept the old deeds.\n\nThe new law empowers officials to settle land ownership, but also permits farmers to defend their property. The prisoners' families have taken their deeds to the provincial capital, and the governor has referred the case to the Ministry of Justice. The commissioners warn of collusion and unrest and ask the Ministry of War to protect the officers involved. Transferring a few officials would allow the affair to pass quietly. A prosecution would make the reform's own agents answer for crimes committed in its name.
english.flavorCNE.7.d: Manufacturers and merchants in [SCOPE.sState('cne_land_reform_industrialists_support_state').GetName] have jointly offered to finance land reform. Workshops are expanding and more carts travel the commercial roads. They want the new law to allow farming families to move freely and bring more workers into the towns.\n\nTheir representatives also seek to submit proposals on land, roads and employment contracts through the Consultative Council. The governor is willing to accept the funding. Officials in the Ministry of Revenue argue that these wealthy men understand industry and could take a greater part in government. The rising manufacturers hope to gain a position in imperial affairs commensurate with their wealth.
english.flavorCNE.7.2: Corporate influence is the real gift
english.flavorCNE.8.d: The streets of [SCOPE.sState('cne_land_reform_peasants_in_city_state').GetName] are filling with newcomers from the countryside. Farming families have sold their land and come in search of wages. Employment brokers send them to factories and building sites, deducting recruitment and lodging charges from their pay.\n\nWorkers have accused the brokers of withholding contracts and enforcing old debts. Manufacturers fear that an inquiry will disrupt recruitment, while local gentry defend brokers linked to their own associations. The governor must decide whether to prosecute the organisations that bind workers to them or leave the disputes to ordinary civil proceedings. In these growing towns, the promise that peasants could leave their old estates and freely earn a living faces its first practical tests.
english.flavorCNE.8.2: Do not intervene in civil disputes
english.flavorCNE.9.2: Do not intervene in civil disputes
english.flavorCNE.10.2: Do not intervene in civil disputes
english.flavorCNE.11.d: Since Mu Zhongtang became Duke of Zhou (President) and State Chancellor of the Great Han Republic in 1818, the military 'tutelary rule' built by this former Western Qin youth officer has traveled a long road. Without question, this young man - once mocked by classmates for admiring Emperor Napoleon of France - has permanently changed the course of history, or at least sharply bent its wheel under the East's Great Unification Movement he helped ignite.\n\nHis contemporaries may never know what future his slogan, 'One Shenzhou state, universal Han soil,' will truly bring. But one of his most striking creations - the Mu dynasty spanning almost all of North China - has come to its end today.
english.flavorCNE.11.f: Defeat made the defeated seem nobler still; fallen Bonaparte appeared taller than standing Napoleon.\n- Victor Hugo
english.flavorCNE.11.1: May this change carry us into a farther age.
english.flavorCNE.12.d: In 1852, Mu Zhongtang, founding emperor of the Chinese Empire, died at the Menghua detached palace outside Bianliang. He was seventy years old and posthumously honored as Gao Emperor of Hua. As one of the most successful military commanders, statesmen, and strategists in Northern Ming China, Mu built a nationalist theoretical framework of lasting influence. Applying those theories, he founded a vast empire across North China, the Northeast, and Mongolia, greatly advanced Eastern industrial modernization, and to some extent inherited and preserved the legacy of the early-19th-century Western Qin Revolution.\n\nBefore his death, Mu foresaw inner-palace struggles among princes and unrest among old intimates such as Su Hong. He entrusted his younger sister Mu Muzi to veteran general Fei Xiyi and urged her to avoid political conflict as much as possible.
english.flavorCNE.12.f: Do not forget your ancestors; cultivate their virtue. Seek to match Heaven's mandate and gain abundant blessing of your own.
english.flavorCNE.12.1: Protect the crown prince and drive back the traitors!
english.flavorCNE.12.2: The crown prince is frail; can he secure the realm? The second prince Mu Chisheng is capable and esteemed - let him rule China.
english.flavorCNE.13.d: After Mu Zhongtang died in early October, his eldest son Mu Chimin proclaimed himself emperor in the eastern secondary capital of Qingdao. He then rushed back to Bianliang and met key succession figures including Prince Ju Mu Chisheng, Grand Chancellor Cha Wanfang, and Central Capital Guard Hua Laishi. The next day, the new emperor summoned all Mu princes stationed across the realm to return for mourning. His true intent was unclear.\n\nOn the night of November 18, when the fifth and sixth princes Mu Chiwu and Mu Chiguang arrived, Mu Chimin suddenly died of heart illness. He named no successor, leaving only two children too young to judge right from wrong. With the throne vacant, the War of the Mu Princes erupted.
english.flavorCNE.13.f: When the ruler is young, the state uncertain, ministers unconvinced, and people distrustful - then to whom should power belong, to your son or to me?\n- Records of the Grand Historian
english.flavorCNE.13.1: By state law, father to son. We must protect the imperial grandson.
english.flavorCNE.13.2: The south is unsettled and Western Qin still stirs. A mature ruler must be enthroned!
english.flavorCNE.14.d:
Mu Muzi, younger sister of Mu Zhongtang, was nearly twenty years younger than her brother. Bright and dignified, she held steadfast loyalty. In Mu's later years she was uniquely favored: above all palace women, and often acting in his place to inspect armies and aid civilians when old Xiangyang wounds limited his mobility. Mu even assigned his capital-camp general Fei Xiyi to escort her, giving the princess great prestige. After Mu's death, she stepped forward to stabilize state affairs and stood among the foremost contributors to succession order.

Yet for the emperor's aunt to hold such authority over palace stability and military-civil peace inevitably reminded powerful old courtiers of Princess Taiping's precedent. In addition, many civil officials in the East Garden outside Bianliang - some nurturing more republican ideals - placed hopes in this populist noblewoman. Ultimately, veteran military elders of the Privy Council agreed to remove her and other unstable elements from decision-making by a 'gentle' method.

Thus, under the 'example' of retiring imperial marshal Fei Xiyi, a group of former capital-camp elders 'escorted' Mu Muzi to reside in the Eastern Continent as a long-term 'traveler.' She never returned to Mu Hua rule again.
english.flavorCNE.14.f: Parting in youth was never light; reunion in old age is sorrow still...\n- Wang Anshi, To the Lord of Chang'an
english.flavorCNE.14.1: Your Highness, this is not my heartlessness - this is state necessity.
english.flavorCNE.14.2: Elder Fei is a pillar of the realm; he cannot simply depart.
english.ce_novelist_desc: The stories written by this character carry a spiritual force and have become a cultural jewel in all human history.
english.bm_the_book: Chronicles of the Northern Ming Warring States
english.flavorCNE.15.t: Publication of Chronicles of the Northern Ming Warring States
english.flavorCNE.15.d: Chronicles of the Northern Ming Warring States is a late-life novel by Mu Muzi, younger sister of founder Mu Zhongtang, written after the Chinese Great Revolution in the Northern Ming world. The work spans five major and ten minor volumes, 480 chapters, and nearly two million characters, with a composition period of thirty-five years. Mu Muzi departed from chaptered-serial conventions and rigid portrayals of princes and generals, drawing on the narrative strengths of classics such as Water Margin, Strange Tales, and Journey to the West to shape characters from every class and stratum of society. In a near-modern historical style, the book recounts over four centuries from the sudden death of Yongle in a 1408 hunt to the 1835 Treaty of Yangzhou and the north-south river partition. Because the work 'bears history's weight while transforming it with the spirit of fiction,' and 'tells both Chinese heroism and old-age suffering,' and is 'required reading for anyone seeking the roots of Asian modernity,' later generations ranked it among the Five Great Chinese Classics and one of the longest novels in human history.
english.flavorCNE.15.f: As Yan and Ming decline, sun and moon fade...\n- Opening verse of Chronicles of the Northern Ming Warring States
english.flavorCNE.15.1: 'Nothing brings greater suffering and fortune to humankind than history itself. Next only to that comes resisting it.'
english.ig_soldier_officials_desc: Qin was once a semi-representative monarchical military state led by soldier-officials and troops, but modern politics no longer permits landholders to monopolize the army. The rank-and-file soldiery class has faded, leaving only the elite soldier-officials.
english.ig_qin_aristocrats_desc: Qin's aristocracy is an alliance of major landowners, decorated military men, and old nobility.
english.ig_ce_mongol_landowners_desc: Mongol nomadic tribes still retain nobility that serves as local administrators in organized nomadic polities, replacing the chiefs and clan heads of more primitive tribal structures. Some lineages can even be traced back to warriors of Genghis Khan's era.
english.ig_ce_mongol_warboss_desc: Mongol nobles who preserve power amid harsh environments and long internal-external conflict are one in ten thousand. Their support represents ancient Mongol tradition.
english.ig_cne_xungui_desc: The Chinese Empire is, in many ways, a progressive form of the ideal Qin-style empire. The officer corps that supported the Mu imperial project earned great merit and thus obtained corresponding power and land.
english.ig_xibei_literati_desc: After the Western Qin Revolution, northern scholars no longer resembled traditional literary gentry; they became a group grounded in practical science and practical politics.
english.FRA_FLAVOR_TEXT: Three cheers to His Majesty Louis I, First Citizen, guardian of European progress and civilization! By him, fields and hills revive; by him, the French have regained both their newspapers and their conscience; by him, a steel-forged future stretches forward under the pulse of steam. And yet this enlightened emperor still has not ushered in the republican age Napoleon once opened in Europe. Like his uncle and adoptive father, he has set an untouchable imperial crown atop popular sovereignty. What awaits such a contradictory nation?
english.GBR_FLAVOR_TEXT: Amid enemies on every side, Great Britain limps into the French century. From New World independence, to revolutionary terror, to Napoleon's rise, and finally the global blockade of the Franco-Ming alliance: Heaven has not favored Britannia. Let fate and sickness depart with old King William. Britain no longer needs imperial mirages; we shall bow our heads, till our fields, and wait for our chance...
english.USM_FLAVOR_TEXT: The age of the Southern and Northern Courts, where Qin, Yan, and Ming contended as three empires, is now yesterday's flower. The Xiangyang campaign that once cut the current of history grows distant. Reforged by reformers Zheng Qin and Chen Dongyang, the Southern Ming polity has entered a new chapter. Industrial trains thunder through the three southeastern provinces, and with them comes ever louder and wilder argument. Where will this nation go? Perhaps the answer to that question will be found at last in the quiet villas of Hangzhou.
english.CNE_FLAVOR_TEXT: 'I would rather die for the broad Zhongxia than serve a lord of partitioned lands.' The revolutionary cries of Chang'an's youth were eventually scattered to ash beneath the cannon thunder of the age. Across the vast North China plain, only one victor still stood: Mu Zhongtang and his overbearing progressive military bloc. Those who betrayed the revolutionary ideal survived only within their own regional customs. Northern republicans and southern gentry-financier interests strangled their dream of unification. Ideals abandoned, people no longer offer themselves - only a crippled land reform remains, and the empire's future grows ever more uncertain...
english.QE1_FLAVOR_TEXT: Even as songs of 'Valiant old Qin, together in national peril' still echo among imperial elites, the people of Western Qin cannot escape the fact that history has cast them aside. More than four centuries after Chen De built his forces in the northwest, this mighty continental empire once came closest to China's mandate - only to shatter against a louder and greater revolutionary juggernaut. Its last hope was ground to dust beneath the hooves of Zhang Baili at the Battle of Dunhuang in 1822. If the surviving western empire wishes to recover in the post-Southern-Northern age, it must face reality and reform with resolve.
english.HUS_FLAVOR_TEXT: The miracle of capital belongs not only to the great powers, but also to free peoples who truly pursue ideals and justice. The courageous uprising of 1644 forged Huaxia East Continent. Over the next two decades, descendants of Sun Chengzong, Li Chengliang, and Nurhaci liberated the entire western coast of the Eastern Continent from a narrow foothold. As the domestic uprisings of Luoyang and Xi'an failed, Eastern civic republicans leaned ever more heavily on this regime, once dismissed as a barbarian Jurchen state. If it can truly establish continental hegemony, its future will be boundless.
english.SIH_FLAVOR_TEXT: Liu Zhongming, lord of Shu, was once merely a commoner. He rose only because Zheng Qin of the Southern Ming court needed a talent capable of checking the western-command Sichuan army. As a result his rule has been cautious and constrained, and this land - once uniquely able to preserve itself through Northern Ming chaos and revolutionary war - missed opportunities for deeper growth in an age of upheaval. Yet the struggles of the realm have only paused, not ended. If the heroes of Sichuan dare to act, they will have their place in the next wave of opportunity.
english.HNA_FLAVOR_TEXT: Zhu Banbo has died in battle. Zheng Diaojin has been exiled. Ye Yincao has retired. Li Hanhan has gone east. Lin Zexu has been reassigned. Chu, once seen as the core of new governance, civic republicanism, and the new Western Command progressives, is rapidly declining and unraveling under the Zheng offensive from the Southern Court. Zhu Jiangchen - bearing prestige, loyalty, and courage - stands isolated and cannot halt the tide. Yet he has not wholly lost. A daring leap in politics, or some other method, may still recover a place for republicanism and the people within Ming.
english.JAP_FLAVOR_TEXT: There was once a brilliant age when the Toyotomi shogunate pacified the Sengoku realm in the east, broke Korea in the north, aided the great powers in the west, and reached the island world in the south. Yet as the Zheng house of Wu rose from equal ally to overlord in the Tang-Ming order, Japan's position became perilous. Over the past century, our land and wealth have been steadily consumed, and we have even lost all of Kyushu. In this era of ever-clearer ambitions from the eastern suzerain, can the famed Taiko shogunate still hold Japan's course in history's storm?
english.GNG_FLAVOR_TEXT: Clan bonds, loyalty, and sage teachings: over centuries in the remote southwest, these principles allowed Zhu's Huai realm to carve prosperity and strength from poor and wild mountain country. Yet regional warlord autonomy may suffice in old times, not in the new age after Northern Ming's end. Huai's western branch never lacked heroes, but to move farther in an age of industry and revolution, we need a spirit greater and more fundamental than heroism itself.
english.PHI_FLAVOR_TEXT: Lin Zexu and Luzon were once models of Southern Ming: one a reform vanguard and student of Xiangyang hero Zhu Banbo, once governing a famed commandery as Governor-General of Huguang; the other a foundational base that sustained Wu's rise and pioneered the examination-representative system. Now that former rising star is suppressed and exiled by Zheng's Southern Court, while old foundations slowly rot in time. What future awaits them?
english.YN1_FLAVOR_TEXT: Far South is Ming's remotest administrative command, with only Kunlunzhou (South Africa) perhaps farther. Yet Far South was also among the first overseas fairylands prized by Chinese settlers. Its vast land yielded strange flora and fauna treasured by physicians and scholars, and over the past two centuries it has become an important lead-and-iron zone for Southern Ming. Though the hot inland deserts slowed settlement and reclamation, technological advance and turmoil in the heartland will keep raising Far South's value as an overseas haven.
english.SHA_FLAVOR_TEXT: Amid ice and snow, the only republican state on Chinese soil stands apart from the world. It was founded by exiles who destroyed the remnants of Qi nobility in their homeland, and has existed for barely two decades. At this edge of a world nearly forgotten by humankind, can they make the republican proclamation pierce storm and blizzard to reach the shore of hope? Or is all this only another glass-like mirage repeating the Great Revolution of Western Qin in Chang'an?
english.PER_FLAVOR_TEXT: The legend of the Gaochang Li house is known across the continent. Descended from Yuan-era Han military magnates, they served Mongol and Han conquerors as warlords between Kokand and Khiva. Through marriages with old Ilkhan lineages and Muslim nobility, they gained favor with Qin's Anxi command and came to dominate all Iran with Qin troops and allied Muslim warlords. Persian society has long grown used to conquest by many peoples, but the Li house cannot think only of surviving the present. As true heirs of Western Qin and loyal followers of the Prophet, they ought to hold a far grander and more just vision for their dynasty and rule.
english.MUG_FLAVOR_TEXT: The Mughal dynasty was once a stout Islamic bastion against the Confucian and Buddhist powers of the East, and even joined all four 'just jihads' against Western Qin. But great empires do not survive on historical glory alone; often they are crushed by the sheer weight of that history. Today's Mughal realm is such a country, with more past than future. Corruption, alcohol, opium, foreign interference, and Southern Ming colonies have pushed its Turco-Mongol ruling bloc toward defeat at an unprecedented speed. Perhaps it should lean further on French aid against the swelling eastern Celestial power - or do the opposite and stand on its own. History, however, will not grant much time for deliberation...

english.ce_culture_event.1.d: More than four centuries have passed since the Chenghua Emperor, who sought to reform the Ming court, died; nearly a century has passed since Li Hezu and Zhao Mingdi launched the first civic revolution. At last, the vast land of Shenzhou stands united under the banner of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName]. The people of this age have achieved immortal merit. Yet our leaders are already looking ahead: what form will this new China take as it stands among the nations of the world?
english.ce_culture_event.1.f: The King of Qin swept through the Six States, what tiger-eyed grandeur! / He waved his sword and split the drifting clouds, the lords all came from west to bow...\n- Li Bai, Ancient Airs (59 poems)
english.ce_culture_event.1.1: With all peoples united, a great nation can be built!
english.ce_culture_event.2.d: Great change has struck the long-divided lands of Ming. The Southern Ming-Northern Hua divide has been broken, and the realm is united again. Since the modern Enligtenment Movement, progressive scholars and civic thinkers have spoken of a new Chinese national identity; now that ideal has entered reality. One of the world's most populous and oldest nations now stands once more beneath one banner, eager to reclaim a rightful place in the world for a unified Chinese state.
english.ce_culture_event.2.f: When ape and man bowed farewell...\n- Anonymous of the Eastern International
english.ce_culture_event.2.1: Is this where Heaven's mandate returns?
english.ce_culture_event.2.2: Let us hope they do not mean to restore a central empire.
english.ce_unification_chinese_culture_desc: With the end of the Northern Ming Warring States age, people have grown weary of endless power struggles among feudal lords, military governors, and warlords. From Li Hezu to Chen Dongyang and Mu Zhongtang, one lesson has become clear: only by unifying the Chinese nation under a modern national identity can final peace be won, rather than returning to old feudal hierarchies. As the old saying goes: 'The Six States fell, the four seas became one; script was unified, axles matched; so it has been for two thousand years.'
english.ce_adult_monarch: Ruler is an adult and not a regent
english.je_ce_unstable_imperium_reason: Since Napoleon III's accession in 1832, the ambitious and intellectually active third-generation Bonaparte emperor has simultaneously pushed for multiple reforms within France, aggressively channeling tax revenue into various 'major industrial sectors.' It seems that by injecting sufficient resources into the industrial economy, he believes all of France, and even Europe, will automatically transform into the 'peaceful and prosperous land' he promised. Can this truly come to pass? And even if France becomes so great, is there a place for the Bonapartes within it?

english.je_ce_subpress_republican_movement_reaso: Since the outbreak of the Great Revolution, an idea of the inseparability of nation and civil rights has been deeply rooted in the French nation, nurtured by the bloodshed and injustice accompanying the rapid development of industrial society. The great Napoleon might have suppressed it with prestige, wisdom, and an iron fist. But he is gone, and France's military and police forces are themselves divided into factions, weakening the power to defend the empire from within. The time for the Republicans has come...
english.je_ce_republican_movement_reason: Since the outbreak of the Great Revolution, an idea of the inseparability of nation and civil rights has been deeply rooted in the French nation, nurtured by the bloodshed and injustice accompanying the rapid development of industrial society. The great Napoleon might have suppressed it with prestige, wisdom, and an iron fist. But he is gone, and France's military and police forces are themselves divided into factions, weakening the power to defend the empire from within. The time for the Republicans has come...

english.ce_french_republican_hit_economy_desc: A just cause never lacks supporters.
english.ce_french_republican_hit_military_desc: Patriotic soldiers should know the nation's interests.
english.ce_french_republican_hit_unity_desc: There are always talents we have not yet discovered.
english.ce_french_republican_hit_status_desc: In this chaotic era, no one in power is without skeletons in their closet.
english.ce_french_republican_hit_local_desc: The people's hearts are the foundation of the movement.
english.ce_french_empire_has_made_choice_tt: An indecisive ruler who has not made a choice before #r December 1838#!
