Today those envoys will witness a fierce eastern conflagration rekindled less than half a century after peace.
english.usm_civilwar.2.f: Alas, Muslims of the world...\n- Popular Account of the Near-Western Wars
english.usm_civilwar.2.1: Raise funds and troops to uphold the new dynasty.
english.usm_civilwar.2.2: Uphold Ming and unite against Wu.
english.usm_civilwar.2.3: Unite against Wu, then establish government by the people.
english.usm_civilwar.2.4: Honour our commitments in the mainland struggle.
english.usm_civilwar.2.5: Watch the fighting and honour our commitments.
english.usm_civilwar.3.d: Local opposition has failed to form a coalition for common war. Provinces and overseas states that remain loyal recognise Zheng rule, while others have left the previous hierarchy. Hangzhou can continue governing the centre, but cannot treat every silence as consent.\n\nThe new dynasty must appoint officials and govern under its constitution, while sustaining authority with the troops and revenues it possesses. Unresolved relations with the provinces and states will be shaped by future development, negotiation and conflict.
english.usm_civilwar.3.d1:
Rather than full explosion of contradictions, decisive Southern Court politicians delayed imperial collapse through firm choices. Even amid Wu-Ming dynastic upheaval, regional governors chose no effective resistance and accepted Wu narratives of total corruption by the Ming emperor and his magnates, preserving a fragile peace in South China.

In one sense, this implies the sun-and-moon dynasty had long become rotten wood no one wished to die with. Zhu Kuobin, the last emperor to defend court order, may simply have been born at the wrong time.

Yet this survivor of four centuries of warlord politics lost much. The age of war-peace confrontation ended, but opponents, regional prejudice among old feudatory populations, and new radical groups still move in the shadows of the new era, cloaking the nation's road forward in dense fog.
english.usm_civilwar.3.f: He who is cursed by ten thousand dies without illness.\n- Ban Gu
english.usm_civilwar.3.2: Should Ming districts everywhere rename themselves now?
english.usm_civilwar.4.d: Zhu Banbo's vision has worn away; Zheng Diaojin's defiance has scattered. Northern princess Mu Muzi once said the bloodstorm at Xiangyang defended only an illusion. It now seems true. Zeng Guofan's firm pacification, Feng Yunshan's defense of Changsha, Chu generals hedging both sides - who can clearly judge their merit and fault? In mortal dust, however, the age of Chu has ended...
english.usm_civilwar.4.d1: Who could have imagined that Sichuan people once most mocking federation restoration would become the final line defending Ming legitimacy? Shu was the safe harbor of four centuries of Northern Ming chaos, yet could not escape slaughter and decline. Old and new Shu commanders alike now turn to mirage beneath Southern Office cannon. Let Wei Jian's last stand leave at least a loyal shadow in history.
english.usm_civilwar.4.d2: A century of sectarian linkage, one morning of shared resolve. Yet against a behemoth ruling half the world from the southeast, courage and strategy still fell one move short. May Huai's famous generals admire Guilin moonlight again in another life.
english.usm_civilwar.4.d3: That stubborn stone by the Yangtze never reached the height teacher Banbo hoped for. Perhaps when we were forced to carry half the Chu army south to Luzon, our result against Hangzhou was already decided. Yet true civic republicans never fear one last gamble if they still hold the people's support. We lament only our own insufficiency, having squandered the blood of the great Ming people...
english.usm_civilwar.4.d4: Western winds disperse, Yunnan colors fade. Our great struggle for independence has reached this unhappy end. At least this country dies pursuing independence, not as burial for some warlord daimyo's campaigns.
english.usm_civilwar.4.d5: Our fronts collapsed through defeat after defeat. Southern Office armies crossed our lands and razed our capital. A hundred-thousand-man force exhausted itself in resistance. In four hundred years of Northern Ming Warring States, a great state's destruction looked no different. We can blame only our own inadequacy.
english.usm_civilwar.4.f: All men must die: some weightier than Mount Tai, others lighter than a feather.\n- Sima Qian
english.usm_civilwar.4.2: I am Wei Mingjian of Guanzhou! If my plan failed, it was Heaven's will!
english.usm_civilwar.6.d: Sometimes history does not favor the prepared. Works built over decades and centuries can burn into smoke and ruins beneath war's thunder and axe. The conquest of Earth undertaken by Wu's supreme rulers in Ming and Eastern name may endure, but their own authority and might have reached the endpoint history assigned today.
english.usm_civilwar.6.f: Jiangnan has many worthy ministers.\n- Book of Southern Qi
english.usm_civilwar.6.1: Under history's gaze, posterity will judge merit and fault. Our task is to ensure there will be a posterity that judges rightly.
english.usm_civilwar.7.d: Sometimes history does not favor the prepared. Works built over decades and centuries can burn into smoke and ruins beneath war's thunder and axe. The conquest of Earth undertaken by Wu's supreme rulers in Ming and Eastern name may endure, but their own authority and might have reached the endpoint history assigned today.
english.usm_civilwar.7.f: All men must die: some weightier than Mount Tai, others lighter than a feather.\n- Sima Qian
english.usm_civilwar.7.1: Can four centuries of foundation be ruined by my hand alone?
english.usm_civilwar.8.t: Dawn of the Great Wu Empire
english.usm_civilwar.8.d: It is time to raise our glorious heads from years of war. Since the dynastic revolution, southern turmoil has finally ended in the best possible way in our hands. That old official vessel which entered Hangzhou harbor 450 years ago has become a colossal warship that breaks all difficulties beneath the waves of the whole world.\n\nBy sweeping away warlords who call themselves loyal and filial, Great Wu at last fulfills the federation reform dream of 'great centralization.' The heroes of Zheng's house can finally remove the mask of loyal service and contend openly among world powers. Better yet, our victory on the world stage was won even before we stepped onto it.
english.usm_civilwar.8.f: Ancient sages contended with dragons and beasts and won...\n- Tang Zhen
english.usm_loss_the_civil_war_tt: Zheng-Wu #bold loses#! the civil war or reaches the #bold North-South partition#! ending
english.usm_civilwar.9.d: This world-shaking farce ended with no winner. In prolonged attrition, east and west of the Southern Court exhausted war potential and industrial foundations alike. Perhaps this fragile peace will soon break and an even greater, bloodier age will come. But for now, at least, we have breathing room...
english.usm_civilwar.9.f: There has never been a good war or a bad peace.\n- Benjamin Franklin
english.usm_civilwar.9.1: Is this the curse of the sun-and-moon nation?
english.usm_civilwar.10.d: The coalition has defeated Wu’s central army. The Ming cause brought the Western provinces and their allies together; victory now raises another question: who will govern from Nanjing?\n\nThe Zhu house still claims the throne, while victorious provincial leaders are reluctant to surrender their military and political authority. Republicans want the citizens who fought together to share in a new deliberative government. Whether the wartime coalition can accommodate these demands will determine the Southern realm’s future constitution.
english.usm_civilwar.10.f: In peace, sons bury fathers; in war, fathers bury sons.\n- Western proverb
english.usm_civilwar.10.1: Restore the Zhu house to government.
english.usm_civilwar.10.2: Retain Ming’s name under our government.
english.usm_civilwar.10.3: Let the people govern without another emperor.
english.usm_civilwar.11.d: The war is over, but its fruits were seized by others. Our relationship with the new regime has become awkward. Since Northern Ming, princely politics in the Central Plains was no novelty. But if today's victor turns guns on us, do we truly have confidence to resist the 'royal host'?
english.usm_civilwar.11.f: Victory and defeat are uncertain in war; to endure shame is the mark of a man.\n- Du Mu
english.usm_civilwar.12.d: Representatives of [SCOPE.sCountry('usm_mister_rebel').GetName] have declared their intention to conduct military, fiscal and diplomatic affairs in their own government’s name. They fought beside the coalition, but now intend to retain their own rule.
english.usm_civilwar.12.f: In our age, true power belongs not to politicians or peoples, but to muskets and cast-iron cannon.\n- Aisin Gioro Minning
english.usm_civilwar.13.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('usm_mister_rebel').GetName] has sent an envoy to swear allegiance and recognise the new centre. The wartime partnership has become a relationship of allegiance, under which local civil and military affairs will now be conducted.
english.usm_civilwar.13.f: In our age, true power belongs not to politicians or peoples, but to muskets and cast-iron cannon.\n- Aisin Gioro Minning
english.usm_civilwar.14.d: One reason we fought through fire and blood for Southern Ming was their promise to return Japanese lands they occupied. Now we have won this great war - it is time for the Ming to honor their pact.
english.usm_civilwar.14.f: Heaven and earth are vast; rule need not belong to one lord alone...\n- Prince Kanenaga of Southern Japan
english.usm_civilwar.15.d: Recent internal turmoil forced us to the negotiating table with the Wa. They demand return of occupied Japanese territories in exchange for helping us win this war. It is a profound humiliation, but we have little choice. Perhaps when conditions favor us later, our armies can erase this shame.
english.usm_civilwar.15.f: The Celestial Court has plans to wage war; small states have plans to resist...\n- Prince Kanenaga of Southern Japan
english.usm_civilwar.16.d: Recent military losses forced us to negotiate with the Wa. They demand the return of occupied Japanese territories as the price for wartime support. It is humiliating, but we have little choice. Next time we occupy foreign lands and fight, we should defend those holdings more actively.
english.usm_civilwar.16.f: The Celestial Court has plans to wage war; small states have plans to resist. In letters we have Confucian moral classics, in arms we have Sun and Wu's stratagems. You may choose your finest generals and elite troops to invade our borders, but in marsh and mountain and island sea we have our own preparations. Why should we kneel in the road and submit?\n- Prince Kanenaga of Southern Japan
english.usm_civilwar.16.2: Outrageous! You merely did your duty!
english.usm_civilwar.17.d: Having defeated our enemies in Southern Ming strife and reoccupied Japanese Kyushu, it is time to issue an ultimatum to the regime that usurped our lands. The Land of the Rising Sun will no longer tolerate this insult to our dignity. The old shogunate's land cession was a mistake.
english.usm_civilwar.17.f: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors onward, China has had rulers - shall the frontier peoples be without them? Heaven and earth are vast, not for one lord alone; the cosmos is broad, and many states may each guard their own sphere. All-under-Heaven belongs to all-under-Heaven, not to one person.\n- Prince Kanenaga of Southern Japan
english.usm_civilwar.18.d: Recent military losses forced us to negotiate with the Wa. They demand the return of occupied Japanese territories as the price for helping us win this war. It is humiliating, but we have little choice. Perhaps next time we occupy foreign lands and go to war, we should defend those lands more actively.
english.usm_civilwar.18.f: The Celestial Court has plans to wage war; small states have plans to resist. In letters we have Confucian moral classics, in arms we have Sun and Wu's stratagems. You may choose your finest generals and elite troops to invade our borders, but in marsh and mountain and island sea we have our own preparations. Why should we kneel in the road and submit?\n- Prince Kanenaga of Southern Japan
english.usm_civilwar.19.t: Wa Forces Exit the Jingnan War
english.usm_civilwar.19.d: With their war aim achieved, Wa forces who once stood with us against Wu are now gradually withdrawing. Their departure will certainly affect the strategic situation.
english.usm_civilwar.19.f: He who understands the times is a true talent; he who adapts is a hero.\n- Yanzi Chunqiu
english.usm_civilwar.20.d: This world-shaking farce ended with no winner. In prolonged attrition, east and west of the Southern Court exhausted war potential and industrial foundations alike. Perhaps this fragile peace will soon break and an even greater, bloodier age will come. But for now, at least, we have breathing room...
english.usm_civilwar.20.2: Perhaps this age has no need for second-rate players...
english.usm_civilwar.21.d: On the eve of the Second Jingnan War's end, [SCOPE.sCountry('usm_opposition_lost_scope').GetNameNoFormatting] declared independence amid chaos. Yet once we established authority in Nanjing, they recognized the gap in strength and legitimacy and chose to join the new central government we formed.
english.usm_civilwar.21.f: He who understands the times is a true talent; he who adapts is a hero.\n- Yanzi Chunqiu
english.usm_civilwar.21.1: Change will come again sooner or later.
english.usm_civilwar.22.d: The war we pushed with all our power has still ended in defeat. Southern Ming - now the Great Wu Empire - proved too strong an opponent. Perhaps only after recovering for a long time in the shadows can our eastern island state pursue independence again. Or perhaps this dissatisfaction with status is merely a darker impulse. In villages and castle towns many voices now say our bloodshed was a tragedy born of greed and tyranny. As a state founded by learning from the great court, we should know contentment.
english.usm_civilwar.22.f: He who understands the times is a true talent; he who adapts is a hero.\n- Yanzi Chunqiu
english.usm_civilwar.23.d: The Southern civil war has brought Kyushu back to the centre of Japanese politics. Zheng ports, trade routes and garrisons on the island support Wu’s maritime power and affect the interests of Japanese lords and merchants.\n\nBoth Wu and its opponents seek Japanese intervention, offering to return the Zheng-held parts of Kyushu after victory. The side we support will determine our allies across the sea and the government from which we must claim our reward.
english.usm_civilwar.23.f: Look across all under Heaven and sea - what lives forever?\n- Oda Nobunaga
english.usm_civilwar.23.1: Support Wu in exchange for its Kyushu holdings after the war.
english.usm_civilwar.23.2: Join Wu’s opponents and seek Kyushu through victory.
english.usm_civilwar.23.3: Remain neutral and make no military commitment.
english.usm_civilwar.24.d: As enemy forces advanced, the final defensive line held by rebel power [SCOPE.sCountry('usm_opposition_lost_scope').GetNameNoFormatting] collapsed at last. Its final organized resistance has ended. Its leaders either died for the state or fled their people in despair.
english.usm_civilwar.24.f: Bodhi has no tree, nor mirror any stand...\n- Huineng
english.usm_civilwar.25.d: One of our important commanders, Lin Hanhan, quietly left surveillance with his family earlier this week and never returned. It is an intolerable scandal. Perhaps we will get our chance to execute this traitor on the battlefield.
english.usm_civilwar.25.f: Good birds choose trees, worthy ministers choose lords...\n- Popular Romance of the Three Kingdoms
english.usm_civilwar.26.d: By proclamation of victory, Zhu Jingyin of Huai - honored by anti-Wu forces as Ming sovereign - has finally ascended as Supreme. This means leaving Guilin and going to Nanjing to enthrone as emperor of Great Ming, like the selected heirs of Huai princes in the old 'Huai-Ning mutual abdication' tradition.
english.usm_civilwar.26.f: The Son of Heaven should be the one with strong troops and warhorses - was he born to it?\n- Old History of the Five Dynasties
english.usm_civilwar.26.1: This may benefit us, but we have our own affairs to handle.
english.flavorJAP_ce.1.d: Ever since the armies of Wu principality aided the late Taikō Toyotomi Hideyoshi in seizing power in Japan, our position has long remained beneath the Southern Ming court led by the prince in Hangzhou. In time, we gradually reduced to that of a vassal and consort to the Ming-nese rule. In the end, not only was Kyushu lost, but the authority over customs and maritime trade was likewise placed under the control of the “Eastern Ocean Consular Office” established by the Chines. Yet fortune has always turned by the change of ages. Amid the torrent of the Southern Ming Federation’s collapse, the current Shogun, [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_ruler').GetIdeology.GetName], seized the pulse of the times and won a hard-earned independence.
english.flavorJAP_ce.1.f: “By command of the Taikun of Japan, we hereby respectfully address His Majesty, Emperor of the Great Chinese Court. From this day forth, Japan shall no longer stand among the tributary states. All matters of territory, governance, military affairs, and commerce shall be judged and administered independently by this country. The old bonds of favor and obligation are not forgotten; yet as Heaven and Earth have changed, so too must names and stations be rectified with the times. May our two countries each keep to their own frontiers, preserve the old amity, and sever the old order.”
english.flavorJAP_ce.2.d: The sweltering heat of midsummer caused the health of the aged [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_shogun').GetPrimaryRoleTitle] [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_shogun').GetFullName] to deteriorate rapidly, and he ultimately passed away earlier this month. His heir, the reform-minded [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_heir').GetFullName], now rules Japan. He has long dreamed of a new and powerful shogunate, and many among the vassals respect this vision.
english.flavorJAP_ce.2.f: “As the summer heat reached its height, our late lord fell gravely ill and at last passed from this world, leaving all the subjects of the realm in mourning. Yet the perilous state of the country permits us no long indulgence in grief. Now that the new lord has inherited the succession, he must restore discipline, strengthen the military, open the path of learning, observe the conditions of all nations, and adopt their strengths, so that the country may be enriched, the army strengthened, and the shogunate renewed. This is no private design for the sake of one house; it is truly a grand policy for Japan for all ages to come.”
english.flavorJAP_ce.2.1: We must learn from the Ming.
english.flavorJAP_ce.3.d: [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_shogun').GetFullName]’s radicalism ultimately proved more than his body could bear. During a sudden outbreak of influenza, he tragically collapsed, never to rise again. As the [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_shogun').GetPrimaryRoleTitle] lay on his deathbed, loyal retainers gathered at his bedside seeking guidance, while conservatives hidden in the shadows began to stir...
english.flavorJAP_ce.3.f: The Shōgun's bed had been moved to face the window. His attendants had hoped the cool air blowing in from the sea would supplement their fans. A chest of ice sat open at the foot of the bed, and a wet cloth across his forehead.\n\nThere was no wind, today. The air rippled beneath the setting sun. Merciless, all-enveloping. He could no longer make out the shape of the waves below.
english.flavorJAP_ce.3.1: “As in the Ming precedent, my brother [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_heir').GetFullName] would be as Yao and Shun...”
english.flavorJAP_ce.3.2: Who would heed the command of a dying [SCOPE.sCharacter('japanese_shogun').GetPrimaryRoleTitle]?
english.state_trait_chenqin_windbreak_project: Legacy of the Poplar Shelterbelt Program
english.nesnd_civic_characters.1.d: Valdieri offers to arrange workshop credit, but asks how military orders and repayments will be secured. His merchant associates expect French connections to sustain trade; local taxpayers fear becoming the final guarantors.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.1.a: Endorse his case for industrial credit.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.1.b: Leave the terms of credit to public debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.101.d: Valdieri continues to press for clear repayment terms on military orders. Manufacturers’ willingness to advance money depends on the guarantees the government will bear. Opportunities opened by French relations must still satisfy the merchants’ accounts.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.101.organisation: Valdieri is no longer active in public life here. Manufacturers still seek guarantees and repayment terms, leaving merchants to judge the treasury’s credit and the government to face the cost of borrowing.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.101.a: Credit needs a basis for repayment.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.2.d: Bellandi moves between a newspaper office and a school for girls, connecting literacy with civic standing. Her republican convictions lead her to question restrictions on education for women and the poor.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.2.a: Endorse her case for access to learning.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.2.b: Leave access to education to public debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.102.d: Bellandi brings the needs of girls’ schools into the press, giving republican debate a concrete question of access to learning. She asks whether those who praise independent citizens will also make room for women and the poor to study.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.102.organisation: Bellandi is absent from the country’s press and public platforms. Access to education for women and the poor remains disputed; funding and admission to girls’ schools still need advocates.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.3.d: Rusciani brings local proposals that leave room for cooperation. He asks governments to settle mining revenues, roads and school obligations before sending more taxes to a common political centre.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.3.a: Endorse the southern case for local revenue.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.3.b: Let local interests make their own case.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.103.t: The South in a Common Budget
english.nesnd_civic_characters.103.d: Rusciani continues to connect southern roads and schools with mining revenue. Local traders seek the markets cooperation might open, but want a common budget to explain which local burdens it will help meet.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.103.organisation: Rusciani is no longer active in public life here. How much southern revenue should remain locally, and who should pay for public services, still shape traders’ judgements of cooperation.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.103.a: Make the local share of common costs clear.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.4.d: Sereni connects unified military command with pay and veterans’ livelihoods. Republican convictions may rally volunteers, but cannot settle their arrears.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.4.a: Endorse his case for military pay and veterans.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.4.b: Let the military case be heard without endorsement.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.104.d: Sereni continues to raise pay and veterans’ livelihoods in discussions of the common military cause. Republican conviction may bring volunteers to the colours; sustained service also requires an answer about military finance and life after discharge.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.104.organisation: Sereni is no longer active in the country’s military politics. Questions of pay and veterans’ livelihoods remain with the forces, and military families still look for a place in public expenditure.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.104.a: Soldiers’ livelihoods belong in the accounts.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.5.d: Vitali accepts the need for reliable public school funding and asks local religious institutions to meet their educational responsibilities. Residents want teachers and affordable lessons, rather than another contest over who owns the school’s name.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.5.a: Endorse the Church’s responsibility for education.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.5.b: Leave responsibility for schools to local debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.105.d: Vitali continues to argue that the Church should bear responsibility for local education. Teachers’ pay and pupils’ fees bring public funding and religious obligations into the same accounts. Families want to know whether they can afford to send a child to school.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.105.organisation: Vitali no longer participates in public life here. Local churches, teachers and pupils’ families still press their claims over fees and funding, keeping responsibility for education in dispute.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.6.d: Martelli brings miners’ injuries and household incomes into public debate. Local industry draws wealth from the pits; workers’ associations demand provision for safety, education and those who can no longer work underground.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.6.a: Endorse the miners’ case for safety and education.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.6.b: Let workers make their own demands heard.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.106.d: Martelli continues to speak for injured miners. Mine revenue can become commercial profit while families of men unable to work struggle for daily subsistence. Workers’ organisations press for safety and education to receive a share of local spending.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.106.organisation: Martelli is no longer active in public life here. Injured miners’ families still depend on their own resources and mutual aid, and the demand that mining wealth help fund safety and education remains.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.106.a: Workers have lives beyond the pit.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.7.d: Tong Shiheng proposes long contracts connecting ports, timber and inland routes. Merchants offer advances in return for dependable revenue. The government must decide what safeguards prevent a concession from becoming another toll on local life.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.7.a: Endorse his case for merchant-financed works.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.7.b: Let the case for concessions face local debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.107.d: Tong Shiheng continues to advocate long contracts linking seaports with the interior. Reliance on private advances makes expected returns a force in the choice of routes, giving local traders reason to scrutinise the concessions.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.107.organisation: Tong Shiheng is no longer active in public life here. Transport between the ports and the interior still ties contractors, local traders and the treasury together; concession terms continue to shape who profits from the roads.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.107.a: The route must serve local livelihoods too.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.8.d: Shen Jichuan collects testimony from bonded families and seeks literacy and association for those already free. Law can end a bond’s force, while the poverty and inherited barriers it leaves behind endure.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.8.a: Endorse his case for education for bonded families.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.8.b: Let the testimony enter public debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.108.d: Shen Jichuan continues to gather the testimony of families bound by debt. Existing law determines the force of their contracts; learning, employment and association shape their prospects. He brings these claims into our country’s dispute over standing and freedom.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.108.organisation: Shen Jichuan is no longer active in public life here. Families bound by debt still face their contracts and the obstacles to education and work; the advocate’s departure has not answered their claims.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.9.d: Bayantu brings pastoral families affected by construction into local negotiations. He seeks passage for livestock and seasonal migration, or compensation for lost pasture. The contractors’ boundaries now reach into the routes by which these families live.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.9.a: Endorse the case for pastoral passage.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.9.b: Leave pasture routes to local negotiation.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.109.d: Bayantu continues to seek passage for seasonal migration. Land a contractor sees as replaceable may connect a pastoral community’s access to water and grazing. Local negotiations must reckon with that route.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.109.organisation: Bayantu no longer participates in public life here. Migrating herds still need passage near the works, and affected families continue to seek protected routes or compensation.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.109.a: Account for the passage of herds and people.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.10.d: Lin Sulan organises evening lessons through immigrant workers’ mutual aid. Literacy helps people read wages, bonds and laws; some employers fear that it also teaches workers to speak for themselves.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.10.b: Let the mutual-aid groups speak for themselves.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.110.d: Lin Sulan continues to promote literacy through workers’ mutual aid. Reading a wage account or debt bond gives workers grounds to challenge an employer’s interpretation, making evening lessons a place for discussion as well as learning.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.110.organisation: Lin Sulan is no longer active in public life here. Workers still seek literacy through mutual aid: wage accounts, debt bonds and laws must be understood, and access to learning still has to be won.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.11.d: Lu Jingduo places the accounts before contractors and local representatives. As an engineer, he asks that payments follow actual work and employment, rather than treating professional standing as a claim to concessions or shares.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.11.a: Endorse public scrutiny of works accounts.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.11.b: Leave the accounts open to public debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.111.d: Lu Jingduo continues to connect payments with work completed and employment. Professional reputation may win a contractor trust, but local interests still want an account of what public expenditure delivers.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.111.organisation: Lu Jingduo no longer participates in public life here. Public works accounts remain before contractors and local interests, who still dispute how payments are made and what the locality receives.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.111.a: Account for the spending and its return.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.12.d: Guan Tingxian asks where the wells’ revenues will go. Concession holders seek expansion; local businesses and residents seek roads, schools and dependable fiscal shares.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.12.a: Endorse the local claim on oil revenue.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.12.b: Let the debate over oil revenue continue.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.112.d: Guan Tingxian continues to ask how much oil revenue should stay where it is produced. Expansion attracts company capital, while roads and schools require local provision. Traders want a voice in the distribution of the proceeds.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.112.organisation: Guan Tingxian is no longer active in public life here. The producing districts still press their claims on revenue and public spending, with oil companies and local traders proposing different uses for the proceeds.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.112.a: The producing districts need a share.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.13.d: Ji Wenheng brings commercial experience into the constitutional debate over examinations. He asks the Assembly of Rites to recognise practical learning and property expertise, while facing the question of whether wealth will become another barrier to ordinary people.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.13.a: Endorse practical learning as a route to public office.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.113.d: Ji Wenheng continues to press the Assembly of Rites to recognise commercial and industrial experience. Those versed in industry and accounts seek a route into public office; established gentry defend the standing of existing qualifications. Examinations must somehow weigh the claims of old and new learning.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.113.organisation: Ji Wenheng is no longer active in public life here. Claims for commercial qualifications still reach the Assembly of Rites, where the weight of practical learning, property and classical study continues to concern new candidates and the established gentry.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.113.a: The Constitution must answer new candidates.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.14.d: Duan Jingchuan, a Sichuan teacher, proposes changes to academy courses and educational places. Teachers seek to impart practical learning, while students hope to proceed from study into public life. Recognition of the curriculum is therefore tied to constitutional qualifications and examinations.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.14.a: Endorse his case for teaching and educational places.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.114.d: Duan Jingchuan continues to take an interest in Sichuan’s curriculum and educational places. Students’ needs give practical learning a constituency; access to national political life still rests on the relevant constitutional and examination procedures.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.114.organisation: Duan Jingchuan is no longer active in public life here. Sichuan’s teachers and students still seek courses and places, leaving the relationship between local education and political qualifications to the relevant institutions.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.15.d: Xu Tingzhang opposes a hurried expansion of public qualifications and arbitrary post-war levies alike. Established elites wish to preserve order, yet cannot ignore how schools, military costs and taxation have changed.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.15.a: Endorse established qualifications and local property.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.15.b: Let the gentry state their own case.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.115.d: Xu Tingzhang still defends established qualifications and opposes arbitrary levies on local wealth. His case appeals to the gentry, but schools, forces and industry still require funds. Defending local interests brings its own obligations towards the public budget.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.115.organisation: Xu Tingzhang is no longer active in public life here. Gentry support for established qualifications and resistance to arbitrary levies remains, alongside the question of how local wealth should support schools and military expenditure.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.16.d: Luo Yingtang approaches literacy through workshop accounts and women workers’ mutual aid. Workers who can read an account can question wages and debts. Their demand for learning reaches from the work sheds towards the academies, bringing educational qualifications into public debate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.16.a: Endorse women workers’ access to literacy.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.16.b: Let the case for mutual aid and education spread.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.116.d: Luo Yingtang continues to approach education through accounts and women workers’ mutual aid. Reading wage accounts and invoices gives workers grounds to speak for themselves. Whether that learning can win public recognition becomes a question of their own.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.116.organisation: Luo Yingtang is no longer active in public life here. Women workers still seek literacy through mutual aid, bringing the prospects opened by that learning before schools and the existing system of qualifications.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.116.a: Let the learners state their needs.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.17.d: Han Shiduo calls for technical education for craftsmen, connecting schools with disputes over wages, injuries and hiring. Manufacturers need skilled hands and workers rely on their skills for a living. Who should pay for training concerns them both.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.17.a: Endorse the craftsmen’s case for skills and livelihoods.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.17.b: Let craftsmen state their own demands.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.117.d: Han Shiduo continues to connect craftsmen’s schools with wages and injuries. Workshops need skilled hands; craftsmen want to know whether training will improve their livelihoods. Technical education has entered the dispute between labour and employers.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.117.organisation: Han Shiduo no longer participates in public life here. Craftsmen’s demands for learning and livelihoods still circulate among workshops: what is taught, who pays for it and what wages trained hands can command remain local questions.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.117.a: Let training lead towards a livelihood.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.18.d: Jiang Shaoheng seeks public budget scrutiny of cross-province works and concentrated capital. Coastal profits, inland taxes and provincial educational places fall on different people; an aggregate total cannot settle their disputes.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.18.a: Endorse public scrutiny of cross-province investment.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.18.b: Let the provinces debate the distribution.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.118.t: What the Provinces Give and Receive
english.nesnd_civic_characters.118.d: Jiang Shaoheng continues to seek scrutiny of cross-province investment in the budget. Coastal profits and inland taxes do not become ownerless when added together. Provincial delegates in the Assembly of Rites must still explain what their own provinces give and receive.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.118.organisation: Jiang Shaoheng is no longer active in public life here. Cross-province works still connect investors and taxpayers, and provincial delegates still face demands to explain the local return in the Assembly’s budget debates.
english.nesnd_c2_person_ita_rusciani_support: The South in a Common Budget: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_ita_vitali_support: The Church and School Fees: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_hus_tong_support: The Reach of a Concession: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_hus_shen_support: The Prospects of Bonded Families: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_hus_lu_support: What Public Money Pays For: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_hus_guan_support: Claims from the Oil Districts: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_usm_xu_support: The Gentry and Local Spending: Endorsement
english.nesnd_c2_person_usm_jiang_support: What the Provinces Give and Receive: Endorsement
english.nesnd_civic_characters.200.d: The constitutional process has recognised practical and provincial qualifications, and Duan Jingchuan has met the corresponding examination requirements. The teacher can now participate as a provincial delegate in the Assembly of Rites, representing educational and public interests. Provincial administrative authority remains separate.
english.nesnd_civic_characters.200.a: Accept the qualification and its responsibilities.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_public_works_: Back military works and provide construction assistance to domestic workshops.
Public Military Works: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_commercial_cr: Support merchant credit for workshops and direct public funds towards local industry.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_local_partner: Support schools maintained with local contributors.
Local School Partnerships: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_reason: French support for the Lombard Republic gave the republican cause a foothold in Italy. Orders for workshops, credit for merchants and funds for schools must still be found within Italy. The army presses for military works, merchants seek dependable repayment, and local contributors want places for their children. The government’s spending will help determine whose needs take priority.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_expense: Workshops and the Italian States Expenditure
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_fiscal_unio: Back pooled revenue and strengthen fiscal administration in the selected state.
Pool Tax Revenue: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_federal_cou: Support local education funding and give the case for retained revenue a basis in school services.
Local Revenue and Schools: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_military_ac: Back public works for military expenditure and veterans, with assistance for local military construction.
Military Accounts and Veterans: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_reason: Building a common Italy means reckoning with the states’ existing military obligations and taxes. Industrial interests favour pooled resources; local traders want revenue kept for schools, and the army puts military accounts and veterans first. A common budget must reconcile these burdens, whether the states pursue unification or negotiate a lasting relationship among themselves.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_chartered_contrac: Back chartered contractors with assistance for local construction.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_open_tenders_desc: Support open tenders and assist local transport infrastructure.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_local_transport_d: Support transport links serving rural communities and local trade.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_local_transport_p: Local Transport Funds: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_reason: The overseas trade associated with Dongqing depends on routes linking ports with inland timber, minerals and farm produce. Large contractors offer capital through concessions that would also deepen their hold on local trade. Smaller firms seek open tenders, while rural communities want connections to their own towns. The government must decide whose needs will shape the continental roads.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_transport_expense: Dongqing and the Continental Roads Expenditure
english.nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_pasture_passage_de: Support passage for pastoral communities. Local infrastructure receives assistance, while construction bears the cost of accommodating pasture routes.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_pasture_passage_po: Protect Pasture Routes: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_land_compensation_: Support compensated development, improving local infrastructure while accepting slower construction.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_frontier_garrisons: Back the army’s proposal to support construction through frontier garrisons.
Garrisons for Construction: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_reason: Railways and mines are reaching into pasture used for seasonal migration. Herds need water and passage; developers need land, and the army wants secure communications. Pastoral communities seek protected routes, developers press for compensated development, and military advocates propose garrisons to support construction. Each course places a different burden on the people who live there.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_labour_schools_: Support education for workers and families bound by debt through school services in the selected state.
Labour and Learning: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_public_accounts: Back scrutiny of public works accounts and assist local fiscal administration.
Publish Public Accounts: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_reason: Families bound by debt bring old obligations and inherited rank with them into the workshops. Teachers and workers seek access to learning; local traders demand to know who benefits from public expenditure. Support for education and scrutiny of public accounts offer different ways into a dispute over freedom and standing that now reaches into everyday working life.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_expense: People Beyond the Debt Bond Expenditure
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_concessions_desc: Back oil concessions and assist construction serving the oil industry.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_royalties_desc: Support the case for local oil royalties and assist fiscal administration in the producing state.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_royalties_politics: Local Oil Royalties: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_oversight_desc: Back workers’ demands for public oversight of oil and direct local assistance towards education.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_oversight_politics: Public Oil Oversight: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_reason: As oil reaches the market, its proceeds become a question of local power. Concessionary companies want to finance further expansion, traders seek royalties for roads and schools, and workers’ organisations demand public oversight. The government must fund the course it chooses as well as count the revenue promised by the wells.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_oil_expense: Oil Wells and Local Revenue Expenditure
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_classical_fran: Support classical learning as the basis of public qualifications and strengthen local fiscal administration.
Retain Classical Examinations: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_practical_fran: Back recognition of practical and commercial learning through assistance to local education.
Admit Practical and Commercial Learning: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_local_franchis: Support wider provincial places and assist the education of prospective candidates.
Broaden Provincial Places: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_reason: The Assembly of Rites draws candidates trained in the classics alongside men versed in machinery, accounts and trade. The cabinet and Six Ministries seek capable officials, while the provinces press the claims of their own students. The weight given to classical qualifications, practical learning and provincial places will shape access to public life under the Constitution and the standing of the established gentry.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_expense: The Constitution and Public Office Expenditure
english.nesnd_c2_usm_schools_practical_schools_d: Support practical curricula in the academies and assist their teaching.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_schools_provincial_schools_: Support wider provincial access to learning through local school services.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_schools_reason: Academy teachers must make room for surveying, machinery and commercial learning alongside the classics. Students seek useful knowledge and a chance to qualify for the Assembly of Rites examinations. Provincial administrators must find the money; provincial delegates bring demands for curricula and places into national debate. Practical teaching and wider provincial access compete for the same education funds.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_industry_coastal_industry_d: Assist construction and industrial operations in coastal workshops.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_industry_inland_industry_de: Direct industrial investment inland and assist local workshop operations through infrastructure.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_industry_reason: Coastal merchants look to ports and shipping when establishing workshops. Inland towns also seek industrial investment, while provincial administrators must answer for local taxes and construction costs. Machinery, labour and goods cross provincial boundaries more readily than those obligations. The government’s choice of where to invest must eventually be borne out in the operation of the works.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_commercial_emp: Support concentrated commercial investment and assist industrial construction in the selected state.
Concentrate Commercial Investment: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_provincial_bal: Back public investment across the provinces and assist fiscal administration in the selected state.
Public Investment Across Provinces: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_scholars_franc: Back broader qualifications for provincial delegates through assistance to local education.
Broaden Delegate Qualifications: Support and Opposition
english.nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_reason: Revenue from industry and trade may return to prosperous commercial centres or support public works across the provinces. The cabinet and Six Ministries plan expenditure; delegates in the Assembly of Rites must answer for what their provinces contribute and receive. Commercial investment, provincial development and access to public office now contend over the gains of industrial growth.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.1.d: The undertaking has stood the test of ordinary operation. The services or production supported by the expenditure now offer tangible results, giving local debate over costs and benefits something concrete to judge.
english.nesnd_c2_retarget_desc: After the present funding term, choose a state within the current borders. Paid costs are not refunded; the new undertaking requires fresh observation.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_agenda: Land and People of the Republic
english.nesnd_c2_italy_agenda_reason: France supports the Lombard Republic, but the Italian states still fund their own armies, schools and administrations. Whether they seek unification or lasting cooperation, they must agree on who will pay for shared undertakings and who will control the money.
english.nesnd_c2_hus_agenda_reason: Workshops, railways and trading houses continue to expand, while debt bonds, inherited privilege and pasture boundaries divide the republic’s freedoms. The government can choose contractors, schools and local distributions; the registration order remains a question for the existing laws and political struggle.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_agenda_reason: The cabinet and Six Ministries propose policy; the Assembly of Rites considers constitutional law. Provincial administrators execute fiscal administration, while provincial delegates represent their provinces. Academy students learn useful arts and prepare for the Assembly’s examinations. Expanding schools and industry sharpens the dispute over who may enter public life and who must pay.
english.nesnd_c2_italian_propose_desc: Each state funds twelve months of expenditure and maintains services in its own schools, administration or military establishments. The other state decides whether to accept. Three months of mutual fulfilment establish an accord. An unanswered proposal lapses after ninety days; talks may resume after twelve months.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.10.t: Schools, Military Revenue and the States
english.nesnd_civic_routes.10.d: A neighbouring state proposes a shared public undertaking. Schools, local revenues and military expenses would become budgetary obligations for both governments. Each must fund services on its own territory. The proposal preserves both states and their borders; the decision is ours.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.10.b: Ask for schools and local services first.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.11.d: The other government is willing to cooperate but asks that schools and local services take priority over military supply. If we agree, both countries will fund these undertakings and maintain the services within their own borders.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.12.d: The states have failed to settle the obligations of this undertaking. Each remains responsible for its schools, revenue and military expenditure; further talks must await another occasion.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.13.d: Both countries have fulfilled the agreement, funding and providing the promised educational, administrative or military services. Cooperation has created shared interests in the provinces and built trust for further negotiations.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_direction_french_republic: Use French support, republican institutions, public works and negotiations among the states to advance Italian integration.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_direction_autonomous_conc: Let the Italian states finance and negotiate cooperation themselves, reducing dependence on French support.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_direction_southern_monarc: Support cooperation under a southern dynasty, bringing local finances and military arrangements into negotiations among the states.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_direction_plural_compact_: Support lasting cooperation in education, church affairs and finance while preserving the governments of the individual states.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_paused: Constitutional deliberation is suspended while the Ming–Wu conflict continues.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_west_open: Western provincial integration remains underway; local works concern current territory.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_west_success: Western provincial integration has succeeded; revenue and military expenditure remain disputed.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_west_fail: Western provincial integration has failed; remaining schools and industry still require support.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_truce: The parties to the truce govern their respective territories.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_wuu: Constitutional law and qualifications under Wu.
english.nesnd_c2_usm_ming: Constitutional law and qualifications under the Ming court.
english.nesnd_hus_transport_reason: This former agenda has ended. Current undertakings depend on their actual arrangements.
english.nesnd_hus_frontier_reason: This former agenda has ended. Current undertakings depend on their actual arrangements.

english.nesnd_usm_distribution_reason: This former agenda has ended. Current undertakings depend on their actual arrangements.
english.je_risorgimento_reason: The Italian states have different governments, armies and foreign ties. The Lombard Republic endures with French support, while republican conviction, dynastic interests and local finances shape the road ahead. The states may pursue unification or lasting cooperation through public obligations.
english.italian_unification.6.d: Italian political mobilisation has changed local government. Established republics and newly organised republican forces seek cooperation, while military costs, revenue and representation remain matters for concrete negotiation.
english.italian_unification.10.d: Italy’s future is debated in schools, barracks and state governments. Support for unification need not entail hostility to France; protection cannot answer local questions of revenue and political standing.
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_federal_cou: Local Revenue and Schools: Local Arrangements
english.nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_military_ac: Military Accounts and Veterans: Local Arrangements
english.nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_practical_fran: Admit Practical and Commercial Learning: Local Arrangements
english.nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_provincial_bal: Public Investment Across Provinces: Local Arrangements
english.nesnd_civic_routes.30.t: Debt Bonds Lose Their Former Power
english.nesnd_civic_routes.30.d: Current law has ended slavery and provides protection for assembly or speech. Debt bonds no longer govern a life in their former fashion, while education, occupations and social standing remain disputed. The consequences of the registration order do not disappear automatically.
english.nesnd_c2_scholarly_exchange_desc: Invite a Sichuan teacher to discussions of curricula and educational places. Independent Sichuan must consent. This changes neither borders nor the person’s home and grants no delegate’s qualification.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.40.t: A Scholarly Invitation from the Southern Court
english.nesnd_civic_routes.40.d: The southern government asks Duan Jingchuan to discuss academy curricula and educational places. Sichuan is independent; this invitation requires its own decision. The teacher’s home and the affairs of local schools remain under this government.
english.nesnd_civic_routes.41.d: Independent Sichuan has agreed to a scholarly exchange with the southern government. Curricula and educational places offer a basis for contact between their academies, while each state retains its own schools. Qualifications for the Assembly of Rites remain subject to its examinations and constitutional procedures.
english.nesnd_c2_italian_abandon_desc: End the current mutual obligations without claiming fulfilment. The original twelve-month expenditure continues to its expiry; negotiations may resume after twelve months.
english.nesnd_c2_productive_levels_tt: For three consecutive months, operating levels in the selected state and production group must reach the total built levels at the start plus the required increase. Market access must be at least 80%. Only building levels with at least 75% employment and a positive weekly profit count; empty or loss-making levels do not.

english.nesnd_wu_eastern_question_reason: The Toyotomi unified Japan with Ming and Wu assistance and fought beside the Zheng in Korea. Their old alliance bound the garrisons in Kyushu to the interests of Japan’s lords. With affairs in the south settled, the court is considering an expedition: send former western officers overseas and establish imperial and Tokugawa governments alongside the Toyotomi, while placing Kyushu and Shikoku under direct Wu administration. The settlement would also reshape overseas garrisons and maritime trade.
english.nesnd_wu_eastern_question_status: Readiness: #v finance and administration, army and government, navy and supplies#!. All three are required to send terms.
english.nesnd_wu_eastern_question_status_offer: The terms have been delivered. Await the Japanese response and the court decision.
english.nesnd_wu_eastern_question_status_war: The intervention is in a [concept_diplomatic_play] or war. Partition requires enforcement of its war goal.
english.nesnd_wu_eastern_question_goal: Settle the negotiations or preserve the current arrangement.
english.nesnd_japan_send_terms_desc: Divide authority among the Emperor, Toyotomi and Tokugawa.
english.nesnd_japan_send_terms_requirements: Nonnegative income and bureaucracy; legitimacy at least 50; army and naval projection at least Japan's; a nonzero fleet with at least 90% maintenance fulfillment. Neither country may be at war or committed to a diplomatic play, nor have a mutual truce. Japan must fully own Kanto, Kyoto, Kansai and Chugoku. Japan must retain a Toyotomi monarchy, with Fu and Wa not yet existing.
english.nesnd_japan_accept_status_quo_desc: Keep the current borders and Japanese government; retain resources for the mainland and other overseas commitments.
english.nesnd_japan_partition_tt: #bold Territorial settlement#!\nJapanese Kyushu and Shikoku pass to Wu. Tokugawa Fu receives Kanto and existing northern Japanese holdings; Imperial Wa receives Kyoto and Osaka. Toyotomi retains the rest of Kansai, Chugoku and Korean holdings. New states become Wu protectorates. An independent Toyotomi state also becomes a protectorate; an existing subject relationship is retained. #v Foreign territory is not transferred.#!
english.nesnd_japan_war_tt: If Japan is a Wu subject, it will become independent as the [concept_diplomatic_play] begins. Wu demands the reorganization of Japan; Japan demands Wu’s humiliation. #v The territorial settlement takes effect only if Wu’s war goal is enforced.#!
english.nesnd_japan_reunification_reason: Alliances across the strait once helped the Toyotomi conquer their rivals and allowed the mainland court to intervene in Japan’s successions, domains and wars. Taxes, armies and commerce now follow competing authorities. [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] must reunite Honshu and secure the freedom to govern its own affairs.
english.nesnd_japan_reunification_status: Unite Honshu under an independent government.
english.nesnd_japan_reunification_goal: Be independent and fully own Honshu’s seven regions: Kanto, Kyoto, Kansai, Chugoku, Tokai, Tohoku and Hokushinetsu.
english.nesnd_japan.1.d: Envoys from Nanjing have brought new terms. Kyoto and Osaka would recognize the Emperor, with a regent conducting the government; the Tokugawa would rule from Edo, the Toyotomi would retain a reduced western domain, and Wu would administer Kyushu and Shikoku directly. The mainland court whose armies helped establish Toyotomi power now proposes to divide it. Retainers have reported the strength and supplies of the garrisons to [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName], who must decide how to answer.
english.nesnd_japan.1.b: Japan shall decide its own affairs.
english.nesnd_japan.2.d: Japan asks the court to withdraw the partition proposal and retain a unified Toyotomi government. The proposed expedition would establish new Japanese governments and divide the forces and revenues now commanded by the Toyotomi. It would also require new arrangements for military spending, shipping and overseas defence. The decision rests with [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullName].
english.nesnd_japan.3.d: The settlement in Japan is in force. The Toyotomi retain Chugoku and the remainder of Kansai; the Tokugawa take Edo and the northern domains. Kyoto and Osaka recognize the Emperor, with a regent conducting Wa’s government. Wu administers Kyushu and Shikoku directly. The new governments take charge of local revenues and armies, dividing the resources once commanded by the Toyotomi.
english.nesnd_japan.4.d: The conflict has ended without implementation of the partition. Fleets and garrisons will redeploy under the existing borders and agreements.
english.nesnd_japan.5.d: Honshu now answers to one independent government. [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] is bringing the revenues and armies of the former domains under common authority. Merchants in the castle towns await a settlement of tolls and taxes as they prepare to trade beyond the old domain boundaries.
english.nesnd_japan.2.d_commander: Japan asks to retain its unified government. [SCOPE.sCharacter('nesnd_japan_commander').GetFullName] has been charged with preparing the expedition. Former western officers will leave the mainland with their commander, supported by the fleet, treasury and allied Japanese lords. Victory would provide territories for the Emperor and Tokugawa. The court must now decide whether to pursue the terms by force.
english.dp_nesnd_eastern_intervention_desc: Wu demands separate Imperial, Tokugawa, Toyotomi and directly administered territories in Japan.
english.gov_nesnd_japan_lin_regency_desc: A monarchy in which a Prince-Regent conducts the government on behalf of the imperial sovereign.
english.nesnd_land_survey_desc: Provide Revenue Ministry funding for workshops and practical schools, helping people leaving the estates learn new trades and take part in industrial growth.
english.nesnd_land_review_desc: Have the Ministries of Justice and Revenue review land disputes and instruct provincial governors to investigate the conduct of reform officials. Farming families should be able to defend the property the new law has granted them.
english.nesnd_land_military_desc: Have the Ministry of Revenue supplement existing relief funds for farming families who have left the estates and have yet to find a livelihood.
english.nesnd_land_suspend_desc: Submit the provinces’ requests to end reform to the Senate and seek a decree closing the campaign.
english.nesnd_crisis.30.a: Review the deeds and suspend the disputed cases.
english.nesnd_crisis.30.b: Have the governor reach a settlement on local terms.
english.nesnd_crisis.30.c: Order the garrisons to surrender their records and punish those who defy the law.
english.nesnd_crisis.30.d: A provincial land dispute has reached the court. Land commissioners have surveyed the countryside under the new law, yet several local military estates still collect rent under the old rules. Farmers who have paid the redemption price are told by their old masters that their fields remain military property and that the dues must be paid. Teachers who helped draft their petitions have been arrested for concealing property.\n\nThe deeds submitted by the affected counties contradict the garrison registers. The provincial governor seeks authority to review the cases, while the commissioners ask the court to send troops to recover the withheld records. As the dispute drags on, farmers gather in the county towns, awaiting an answer from the government that promised to free them.
english.nesnd_crisis.33.a: Dismiss the officials, provide compensation and reopen the case.
english.nesnd_crisis.33.d: Veterans, local scholars and dispossessed farmers in Shanxi have gathered over the hardship and arrests that followed the land surveys. Republican organisers use village schools and old military connections to circulate petitions, calling on each county to choose delegates and hold officers accountable for the seizure of farmland.\n\nSeveral garrisons refuse to surrender the accused officers and have turned away the governor's investigators. The county delegates demand the removal of the chief commissioner, a fresh review of titles and compensation for the injured farmers. Republican organisers are seeking allies among the troops and preparing to rise if their petitions fail. The Ministry of Justice has referred the case to the court: dismiss the officials and reopen the inquiry, or prosecute the assemblies for defying the law.
english.nesnd_crisis.31.a: Settle provincial powers and preserve their allegiance.
english.nesnd_crisis.31.b: The armies now answer to their own masters.
english.nesnd_crisis.31.d: Field commands across the Empire are withholding taxes owed to the Ministry of Revenue. Officers seize customs posts, granaries and provincial offices in the name of paying their troops. Governors either yield to the garrisons or use their own loyal units to contest the revenue. Land commissioners can work only where the troops permit them, while unpaid soldiers demand estates from their commanders. The military blocs have acquired powers far beyond their former holdings.\n\nRedeployment orders issued by the Ministry of War in the name of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullNameWithTitle] are repeatedly returned. Senior members of the Senate demand recognition of the military and fiscal powers already seized by governors and commands in exchange for their continued allegiance. The court can no longer hear the provincial petitions forwarded by the Consultative Council. Without a settlement, commands beyond its control may establish governments of their own.
english.nesnd_crisis.32.a: Issue the decree and bring the land revolution to a close.
english.nesnd_crisis.32.d: Memorials requesting an end to land reform have reached the court. The senior commanders and ministers of the Senate propose a compromise and ask [ROOT.GetCountry.GetRuler.GetFullNameWithTitle] to close the campaign by decree. Under their draft, land recognised by the new deeds would remain with military households, who must promise lower rents and allow tenants to leave for work. Unsettled estates, military land and lineage property would pass under the governors' supervision as state lands let to tenants.\n\nThe proposal humiliates the ministers who championed reform. It would also restore a place in taxation and village government to the local powers sustained by the old land system. The Ministries of Revenue and War hope to settle the provincial disputes and return scarce funds and officials to ordinary administration. Approval would bring the land revolution to an end on these terms, leaving its remaining ambitions to another generation.
english.nesnd_huguang_preparations_reason: When Zhu Banbo reorganised Huguang, he repaired the fortifications of Xiangyang, brought young officers into teaching, and exchanged military ironware for grain from Sichuan. Wounded and retired soldiers entered supply services and farming garrisons. Republicans who remained in Xiangyang helped the governor-general reform Yuelu Academy. Over twenty years, the army, land revenues and academies became closely bound to his government, with Chen Dongyang supporting it at court. Xiangyang’s troops came to be regarded as the leaders of the New Western Administration, an indispensable pillar of the Southern Ming federation.\n\nThe Zheng family once supported Zhu Banbo vigorously. Now it repeatedly accuses Xiangyang of withholding taxes and concealing households. Southern officers friendly to Huguang, including Shi Yuanfu and Lin Hanhan, have been posted away, while our republican allies at court face exclusion. We must prepare for the worst: reassess the soldiers and farming households of the garrisons, restore grain shipments from upriver, and win over the academy students who will soon enter political life.
english.nesnd_hna_academy_button_desc: Yuelu Academy in Xiangyang is the intellectual centre of Huguang’s officials and aspiring politicians. Its students study and debate public affairs before taking the examinations of the Assembly of Rites to enter Southern political life. Loyalty to the Southern realm has guided their education since the academy’s foundation. With the Southern Administration pressing us at every turn, its teachers must distinguish the Zheng rulers who dominate the government from the Zhu imperial house. Students won over in the lecture hall today may stand with us as provincial delegates tomorrow.
english.nesnd_hna_supply_button_desc: Huguang’s workshops and Sichuan’s grain boats sustained Xiangyang when we fought the Mu forces. As the divide between the Southern and Western Administrations deepens, we should renew our contacts in Sichuan, coordinate arms and grain supplies between the two provinces, and reopen the wartime depots along the river. If the ministers who threaten us make their move, Xiangyang must have food and weapons.
english.nesnd_hna_veterans_button: Call the Veterans’ Assemblies to Readiness
english.nesnd_hna_veterans_button_desc: Under Zhu Banbo, Chu soldiers enjoyed better conditions than their Southern allies. He also borrowed northern practices of fixed service terms and veterans’ assemblies, sending trained former soldiers to lead farming settlers and rebuild communities exhausted by war. These assemblies are now well established. Their veterans know both the army and the countryside; calling them together to organise food, relief and supplies will give wartime mobilisation a firm local foundation.
english.nesnd_federal_compact_button_desc: Reform has carried the Southern realm beyond the old order of military fiefs. Hangzhou can no longer decide its government alone. Provincial delegates will debate appointments, taxation, military funding and provincial powers in the Assembly of Rites, while the cabinet and Six Ministries must govern under the revised constitution. We should first seek support from the Western provinces and overseas states, allowing the Zhu sovereign to govern constitutionally, free of the Southern Administration’s domination.
english.nesnd_protect_chen_button_desc: Chen Dongyang’s reforms threaten the estates and titles of gentry, former feudal lords and military officers. Master Dongguan may be fearless, but the court cannot disregard their hostility. Assign dedicated guards and consider keeping him at his residence or investigating insiders, preserving the leader needed to sustain reform.\n\nProtection lasts #v six months#!. Without dedicated guards, the case has death, injury and escape chances of #v 40/25/35#!. Funding and renewal terms appear in the protection proposal.
english.nesnd_crisis.10.a: With law as its foundation, the state can stand!
english.nesnd_crisis.10.t: The Memorial on Constitutional Administration in the Provinces and Garrisons Is Adopted
english.nesnd_crisis.10.d: Provincial delegates in the Assembly of Rites have supported the new provisions on appointments, land taxation and military funding, incorporating them into Southern Ming’s constitution. The Zhu succession endures, and the powers of the centre and provinces now rest on an accepted legal foundation.\n\nChen Dongyang’s restoration of provincial administrative commissions enabled common civil and military administration without fully resolving the status of former feudal lords and their local powers. Facing the northern advance, the Southern and Western Administrations had joined their armies to suppress resistance. Disputes then postponed by war have at last received a constitutional settlement.
english.nesnd_crisis.11.a: Publish the findings and pursue the investigation.
english.nesnd_crisis.11.b: Investigate in secret, and spare no one!
english.nesnd_crisis.11.d: The chief minister’s guards have intercepted a forged order changing the watch. The Embroidered Uniform Guard and Court of Judicial Review arrested its bearer and accomplices. Chen Dongyang was taken to safety and returned only after the suspects had been secured.\n\nThe investigation then implicated officials handling military procurement and shipping, together with their contacts among provincial gentry and former feudal lords. The Court of Judicial Review favours disclosure to expose their official connections; the Embroidered Uniform Guard insists on secrecy to avoid alerting suspects still at large. The cabinet must decide how to proceed and bear the political consequences.
english.nesnd_crisis.20.a: Put our own country in order first.
english.nesnd_crisis.20.c: Contact the Xiangfan garrison and prepare to march south.
english.nesnd_crisis.20.t: A Pretender Takes the Southern Throne
english.nesnd_crisis.20.d: News that the despised Wu have cast off Ming and claimed the throne has brought celebration among ministers north of the river. Some recall the Mu sovereign’s great southern expedition. If the pretenders are consumed by fighting the Western provinces, a new campaign might reunify the realm in a single stroke.\n\nFrontier commanders have requested funds and contacted “men of understanding” in Huguang. Yet our own realm is far from settled. Domestic government still requires troops and money; unfinished land reform would make a southern expedition more burdensome still. What could the empire gain by entering this struggle now?
english.nesnd_crisis.21.d: Zheng fleets, trading houses and dependencies have carried news of the Southern war abroad. Merchants fear the seizure of their cargoes, while envoys from the rival sides seek recognition, military supplies and loans.\n\n[ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] has interests of its own in these exchanges. Keeping trade open requires dealings with those who control the ports and sea routes. Receiving exiles or supplying the anti-Wu forces would draw us more deeply into the Southern political struggle.
english.nesnd_crisis.40.a: Judge cases individually and retain local talent.
english.nesnd_crisis.40.b: Purge the old parties and rebuild military rule.
english.nesnd_crisis.40.d: With the fighting ended, local civil and military authority is passing under Wu rule. The new dynasty must now govern: production and trade disrupted by war must recover, people need their livelihoods, and officials and scholars who opposed Zheng will not disappear with defeat.\n\nHangzhou’s accumulated military and fiscal strength can sustain reconstruction. We may judge opponents individually and retain experienced local officials, or use victory to purge the old parties and make the army the foundation of the new order. These decisions will show the realm what government in the Zheng family’s own name means.
english.nesnd_crisis.41.a: Reorganise government and the armed forces.
english.nesnd_crisis.41.b: Reward the armies according to custom.
english.nesnd_crisis.41.d: The troops are returning from abroad. Local lords demand the rewards promised when they joined the campaign, merchants want shipping restored, and the government must arrange its garrisons and revenues.\n\nThe mainland war has given [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] an opportunity to reorganise. More consistent taxation and official training would strengthen central administration; honouring military claims first would secure the commanders and lords on whom the expedition relied.
english.nesnd_early_accession_desc: The Southern Administration commands the realm’s troops and revenues. Rally ministers supporting Zheng, petition the Ming court for abdication, and demand a response from the provinces and overseas states.

english.nesnd_crisis.11.f: “Hold the prisoners separately and secure all correspondence. Tomorrow, the cabinet will return to the case.”
english.nesnd_crisis.30.f: “The garrison says the land belongs to the army. The county says it belongs to the state. We ask only this: what did our payment last year redeem?”
english.nesnd_crisis.33.f: “When we marched, they said we were fighting for land to farm and a hearing for every grievance. Back in our own villages, we have to ask for it all again.”
english.nesnd_crisis.31.f: “This province pays the troops and this province feeds them. If the ministers cannot send our wages, they must let us raise the money ourselves.”
english.nesnd_crisis.32.f: “Lower the rents, let the tenants travel, and preserve the old holdings. Perhaps the garrisons will then end their resistance.”
english.nesnd_crisis.10.f: “Let every province and garrison act according to the constitution.”
english.nesnd_crisis.20.f: “Some men who crossed the river in the former campaign remain in service. If Your Majesty considers another march south, let us first assess the grain and pay.”
english.nesnd_crisis.21.f: “The cargo is loaded. We await only your answer: will the old trading papers still be honoured?”
english.nesnd_crisis.40.f: “The provinces need work and commerce restored, so that soldiers and civilians can support themselves.”
english.nesnd_crisis.41.f: “Every house still holds its promises from the expedition. Now that we have returned, we must settle them together.”
