english.lawgroup_nesnd_hus_social_hierarchy_desc: A system that assigns social standing within the republic by cultural registration.
english.nesnd_hus_social_hierarchy_desc: Han, Manchu and Mongol, Indigenous American, and European registrations determine acceptance and treatment within the republic.
english.law_nesnd_hus_four_tier_system_desc: Han people occupy the first tier, Manchu and Mongol peoples the second, Indigenous Americans the third, and Europeans the fourth. Cultural registration limits social standing regardless of wealth or profession.
english.law_nesnd_hus_manchu_registration_desc: Manchu and Mongol residents receive the same first-tier registration as Han residents. Indigenous Americans remain in the third tier and Europeans in the fourth, as the republic enlarges the body entitled to its highest standing.
english.law_nesnd_hus_native_registration_desc: Indigenous Americans receive the same first-tier registration as Han residents. Manchu and Mongol residents remain in the second tier and Europeans in the fourth. Equal civic standing reshapes the relationship between settlers and Indigenous peoples.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_reason: Citizenship has never carried equal weight in the $HUS$. Han residents stand first, followed by Manchu and Mongol peoples, Indigenous Americans, and Europeans. Living in the same republic does not bring the same treatment. The question of widening the civic body has now reached the government. Manchu and Mongol residents seek equality through their ties with the Han; Indigenous peoples demand recognition of their claims upon this land and its republic.\n\nThe government will grant first-tier registration to one of these groups after a year of registration. Its decision will also reshape relations with those left under the old distinctions.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_goal: Choose whom to admit to the first tier and complete a year of registration.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_lock_tt: $lawgroup_citizenship$ laws cannot be changed while the Dongzhou social hierarchy remains in force
english.nesnd_hus_registration_enacted: Registration is complete and its law is in force
english.nesnd_hus_registration_choose: The government has yet to decide whom to admit to the first tier.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_pending_manchu: Manchu and Mongol registration is underway.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_completed: Registration is complete and the new law is in force.
english.nesnd_hus_registration_conflict: Conflicting registration decisions have left the existing hierarchy in place.
english.nesnd_hus_register_manchu_desc: Ties between Manchu, Mongol, and Han residents offer one path to a broader civic body. The government will recognize their equal social standing.
english.nesnd_hus_register_manchu_tt: $law_nesnd_hus_manchu_registration$ takes effect after #bold 12 months#!. Indigenous Americans remain in the third tier and Europeans in the fourth. This choice cannot be changed.
english.nesnd_hus_register_native_desc: Indigenous peoples share the republic’s land. The government will recognize their equal standing with Han residents, prompting Manchu and Mongol residents left in the second tier to seek a life elsewhere.
english.nesnd_hus_register_native_tt: $law_nesnd_hus_native_registration$ takes effect after #bold 12 months#!. Manchu and Mongol residents remain in the second tier and Europeans in the fourth; Manchu and Mongol communities will subsequently leave for $CNE$ or the American West. This choice cannot be changed.
english.nesnd_hus_registration.1.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_khanate').GetName] has been established. Indigenous communities from Dongzhou and the United States are settling there, looking to their new khan to defend their lands. Washington and the government of Dongzhou reject the loss of this territory. War on the Plains is imminent.
english.nesnd_hus_registration.1.a: A new government stands on the Plains.
english.nesnd_hus_registration.2.d: After Indigenous registration was completed, Manchu and Mongol residents remained in the second tier. They have now left the republic: some for $CNE$, others for the American West, seeking a life on new ground.

english.nesnd_south_pressure_detail_tt:
#bold Succession Pressure#!: #v [Country.MakeScope.ScriptValue('nesnd_south_pressure_value')|1] / 100#!
Monthly change: #v [Country.MakeScope.ScriptValue('nesnd_south_monthly_pressure_value')|1]#!. Pressure rises by #n +3#! each month, or #n +2.5#! under the Constitutional Settlement. Active reconciliation reduces it by #p 3#!.

#bold The First Minister's Case#!
From #v July 1837#!, the case may begin when pressure exceeds #v 24#!. From the beginning of #v 1838#!, an unresolved case involving Chen Dongyang, if he remains in the country, leads to the assassination and protection events. His death adds #n +25#! pressure, injury #n +10#!, and escape #n +3#!.

After the case is resolved, #v 70#! pressure permits an early accession. At #v 100#!, succession proceeds if Zheng Qin has departed. From the beginning of #v 1839#!, an unresolved dynastic dispute rises to #v 100#! once the First Minister's case has concluded. Succession and the other states' responses then proceed whether or not Zheng Qin is still alive. A peaceful settlement ends the dispute.
english.nesnd_south_compact_detail_tt:
#bold Support for the settlement#!
Mainland, overseas and Japanese governments account for #v 50%, 30% and 20%#! respectively. Commitments last #v 36 months#! and cease to count after a change of alignment or overlord, war against the centre, or withdrawal.

#bold A peaceful constitutional settlement#!
The chosen side needs political support of #v 85#! and a lead of #v 20#!, sustained for #v 12 months#!. Ming needs #v 75%#! commitment support and at least two mainland core governments. Wu needs #v 80%#!, consent from every government due for integration and the Japanese territorial parties, and a sufficiently prepared fleet. A completed settlement ends the dispute.
english.nesnd_chen.1.d:
Chen Dongyang came to Southern Ming as an exile from Western Qin and joined King Zheng Qin of Wu in reforming the state. Guoren republicans thereby entered the heart of Southern government. Reform now threatens the estates and titles of gentry, former feudal lords and officers; hostile verses and threatening letters continue to arrive. Master Dongguan remains absorbed in public affairs, but the cabinet cannot entrust his safety entirely to old alliances.

The court may fund a personal guard, keep him at his residence, or investigate his attendants and contacts. Protecting the leader of reform will cost money and place more power in the hands of the cabinet directing his guards.

The cabinet has assigned dedicated guards to Chen Dongyang’s residence and journeys, with their wages paid weekly.

english.nesnd_chen.1.f: Sustain the living, establish the people, and order their livelihoods.\n— Chen Dongyang, On the Great Nation
english.nesnd_chen.1.a: Place the guard under the Cabinet and pay it from the treasury.
english.nesnd_chen.1.b: Remain in the guarded offices and postpone the eastern journey.
english.nesnd_chen.1.c: Investigate the accomplices and those who recommended them.
english.nesnd_chen.1.e: Withdraw the special guard and restore the usual arrangements.
english.nesnd_chen.guard_tt: Pay @money!#v 12,000#!, then @money!#v 500#! per week and #v 40#! [concept_authority] for six months. Death/wounding/escape chances for this plot: #v 15/25/60#!.
english.nesnd_chen.residence_tt: Pay @money!#v 24,000#!, then @money!#v 1,000#! per week and #v 80#! [concept_authority] for six months. Death/wounding/escape chances: #v 10/20/70#!.
english.nesnd_chen.intel_tt: Pay @money!#v 18,000#!. Armed Forces [concept_approval]: #n −2#! for six months. With an active guard and investigation, death/wounding/escape chances are #v 8/22/70#!.\n\nThe investigation lasts at most six months. Withdrawing the guard, Chen's death, or resolution of this plot ends it as well. The investigation’s protection ends when the guard expires, Chen leaves the country or the Ming-Wu crisis ends. Renewing the guard does not extend the investigation.
english.nesnd_chen.3.d: Chen Dongyang was attacked aboard the vessel carrying him east to lecture. A shot passed through his shoulder and arm. His attendants took him below and summoned a physician. Only after nightfall did his waiting students hear that he was still alive.\n\nThe veteran of the Western Qin revolution and the southern reforms now lay wounded. His followers published accounts of the attack and demanded an inquiry into the escort. Provincial correspondence questioned the Southern Command’s shipping arrangements, adding the bloodshed to the struggle over reform and political authority.
english.nesnd_chen.3.f: Take the boundless world as the outer wall, and the right path as the inner city.\n— Chen Dongyang, On the Great Nation
english.nesnd_chen.3.a: Attend to his wounds and continue the affairs of state.
english.nesnd_chen.wounded_tt: Chen Dongyang is wounded. Armed confrontation rises by #n 10#!. This plot is concluded and the special guard costs end.
english.nesnd_chen.4.d: Before Chen’s vessel departed, a boatman noticed that a food box had been resealed. The attendant who handled it named his contact. Letters recovered from the contact’s rooms implicated officials who had arranged the journey. The landing was closed and Chen returned to his offices with his students.\n\nParty conflict had eroded the old alliance between the Western Qin exiles and the Zheng command. The attempted murder made Chen’s movements a matter of public debate across [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName]. Republicans continued publishing in his name, while the Cabinet investigated the prisoners and the appointment of the escort.
english.nesnd_chen.4.f: Even one city, one enclosure, one small corner may still be a great nation.\n— Chen Dongyang, On the Great Nation
english.nesnd_chen.4.a: Resume the sitting and appoint an inquiry.
english.nesnd_chen.escape_tt: Chen Dongyang survives this plot. Armed confrontation rises by #n 3#!. This plot is concluded and the special guard costs end.
english.nesnd_chen.3.residence: A shot rang through the guarded offices. Chen fell beside his desk and lost much blood before the physician removed the bullet. The watch sealed the gates. His students waited outside until dawn for word that he had regained consciousness.\n\nHis followers published accounts of the attack and demanded to know how the assailant had entered the residence. The Cabinet had assumed responsibility for its security. The appointments, recommendations and handovers inside the compound would now be examined by the court.
english.nesnd_chen.4.residence: The watch found a replaced seal on the evening food box and detained the attendant who carried it. His recommendation identified an address where investigators recovered letters and a packet of medicine. Chen remained indoors until dawn, when he learned what had happened.\n\nParty conflict had eroded the old alliance between the Western Qin exiles and the Zheng command. The attempted murder made Chen’s movements a matter of public debate across [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName]. Republicans continued publishing in his name, while the Cabinet examined the appointments and recommendations within the residence.
english.nesnd_chen.death_residence_desc: Chen postponed his journey and continued working in the guarded offices. Two signatures accompanied the medicine brought from the kitchen, but its seal had been replaced. By the time the physician arrived, Chen could no longer speak.\n\nAt dawn the Cabinet sealed the bowl and the duty register. The southern reformers had lost their leader. Provincial delegates gathered outside, waiting for the appointment of a successor.

english.nesnd_chen.finance_rules: #bold Funding conditions#!\nPurchase or renewal requires sufficient [concept_gold_reserves], no [concept_default], and no continuing post-[concept_bankruptcy] penalty. Guards can be renewed after five months; an active guard also permits a separately funded investigation.

english.nesnd_cne_confidence_journal_reason: The fires of the Great Revolution have faded, but its promises still guide clerks, junior officers, soldiers and peasants seeking release from old obligations. They see the land revolution as the continuation of an unfinished cause.\n\nAfter Mu Zhongtang became emperor, the Six Ministries administered the state, while founding commanders and senior ministers in the Senate monopolised legislative power. The Consultative Council gathers petitions and makes proposals whose fate rests with those who govern. Republican exiles in the south and northwest call Mu a traitor. Many supporters of reform still regard him and his companions as champions of enlightenment and progress. Imperial policy depends on the surviving enthusiasm of these officials, soldiers and farmers. Each new survey, change of occupation and reorganisation of the estates asks them to endure more.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence_status: The provinces still trust the court to fulfil the unfinished promise of the Great Revolution.
english.nesnd_cne_republic_journal_reason: Republican promises once united scholars, soldiers and villagers beneath one banner. The restoration of an imperial throne divided those comrades into rulers, subjects and exiles. Now the republicans have risen again to complete the unfinished revolution.\n\nThis war cannot end in a lasting partition. Unless the republican armies overthrow the imperial government, their provincial coalition will crumble. If they seize most of its provinces, they can inherit the Empire and proclaim the Han Commonwealth.
english.nesnd_cne_republic_status: While at war with the Empire, directly control at least #v 80%#! of its states to annex it and restore the Commonwealth. Both sides demand annexation.\nIf the war ends while the Empire still exists, the republican cause fails and its territory is annexed by the Empire. Victory grants claims on the parts of Hunan, Hubei and Sichuan outside the Commonwealth and its subjects.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.1.d: Republicans in the north have risen. Officers and provincial organisers have proclaimed the Han Republican Army, accusing the court of betraying the Great Revolution. The people who once sustained land reform are dividing against one another.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.1.a: Gather the armies still loyal to the court.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.2.d: The provincial coalition has taken up arms. Its government rejects the imperial throne and pledges to rebuild the Han Commonwealth. Some officers remember marching beside Mu Zhongtang; now their banners advance against his Empire.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.3.d: The imperial government has fallen. The republicans have taken over its provinces and offices and established the Han Commonwealth. The new government reasserts the revolutionary claim to national unity in those parts of Hunan, Hubei and Sichuan still outside its own rule or that of its subjects.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.4.d: The republican coalition can no longer sustain its war. Its provinces return to imperial rule. The fighting has ended, though the questions raised by the rebels remain.
english.dp_nesnd_cne_republic_desc: The Empire and republicans contest the northern provinces.
english.dp_nesnd_cne_republic_tooltip: Both sides demand annexation of their opponent.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.5.republic: The monarchy has ended, and with it the political settlement behind Emperor Mu’s land revolution. The new government inherits the offices and their records; the future of fields, towns and military estates now rests with a different order.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.5.war: Civil war has broken out. Provincial administrations and armies now answer to rival governments. Military orders have displaced the work of land reform, and the court can no longer carry out the campaign.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.5.coup: A coup has changed the balance of power at court. Reform officials have been recalled and the provinces await new orders. The movement begun in Emperor Mu’s name has lost its political foundation.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.5.exhausted: The enthusiasm of the Great Revolution has faded. Officials will no longer promise another transformation; soldiers and villagers no longer trust the assurances they once embraced. The court can still issue orders, but the movement has spent its strength.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence.5.a: End the reform and close its programmes.

english.nesnd_cne_land_journal_reason: Military nobles and local lineages hold estates that bind farming families to old patrons. Marketable land opens agriculture to new investment, but a sale does not provide a livelihood for those displaced. Employment and migration must follow the change in ownership.
english.nesnd_cne_land_start_button_desc: Survey fields and open land transfers, freeing land and peasants from clan control.
english.nesnd_cne_land_stop_button_desc: Suspend land surveys and transfers and recall the officials responsible.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_journal_reason: People leaving the estates need work in workshops, mines and towns. Coal and iron must sustain the production of steel, tools and engines, while relief helps workers endure illness, unemployment and old age. The industrial, educational and welfare measures discussed by the Six Ministries depend on governors to organise and carry them out. The occupations and learning that grow with the cities will also weaken the authority of the old rural schools and scholars.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_start_button_desc: Expand workshops, mines and towns, with relief for the workers arriving there.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_stop_button_desc: Suspend the state-sponsored resettlement and urban expansion programme.
english.nesnd_cne_camps_journal_reason: Since 1444, the Qin military colonies of Northern Ming have developed into an estate system across the north. Land supplied the army's food and pay, while the army sustained taxation and conquest. Military and agricultural interests grew together. Bringing these lands and mines into civilian use now threatens entrenched military privileges.\n\nThe Ministry of Revenue wants the estates brought under ordinary taxation and management. The Ministry of War must answer officers who invoke unpaid wages and past service. Governors charged with enforcing the law may lack the force to compel their garrisons, while the founding commanders in the Senate are reluctant to surrender their own property. The provinces can proceed separately and suspend reform where disputes become unmanageable. New revenue and production must eventually replace the army's landed income.
english.nesnd_cne_land_status: $nesnd_cne_land_requirements$\nEstablish peasant proprietorship, commercialised agriculture or collectivised agriculture.
english.nesnd_cne_start_requirements: Land reform remains active; nonnegative bureaucracy, no bankruptcy penalty, disorder below 65, and ownership of the state.
english.nesnd_cne_land_requirements: Research Intensive Agriculture; developed agricultural land must occupy at least #v 6%#! of arable capacity in the reform regions; non-negative bureaucracy, no bankruptcy, disorder below #v 65#!.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_requirements: At least #v 5#! states with level-#v 5#! urban centres; iron mines #v 25#!, coal mines #v 40#!, steel mills #v 10#!, tooling workshops #v 30#!, motor industries #v 6#!, logging camps #v 60#!, shipyards #v 12#! levels.\nUnlock welfare technology, enact Poor Laws, Wage Subsidies or Old Age Pension, and fund Social Security to level #v 1#!; non-negative bureaucracy, no bankruptcy, disorder below #v 65#!.
english.nesnd_cne_land_start_tt: Monthly reform progress #p +0.25#!. Landowners approval #n −2#!, Rural Folk approval #n −1#!; Landowners attraction #n −15%#! and Industrialists attraction #p +15%#!. Enactment success #p +5 percentage points#! and minimum wage #p +5%#!. Costs #n 5#! public confidence per year.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_start_tt: Monthly reform progress #p +0.35#!. Devout approval #n −2#!, Industrialists approval #n −1#!; Petite Bourgeoisie attraction #p +15%#!. Enactment success #p +5 percentage points#! and minimum wage #p +5%#!. Costs #n 5#! public confidence per year.
english.nesnd_cne_land_stop_tt: End the progress, confidence cost and temporary modifiers of land commercialisation.
english.nesnd_cne_urban_stop_tt: End the progress, confidence cost and temporary modifiers of urbanisation.
english.nesnd_cne_camp_start_tt: This state adds #p 0.05#! reform progress monthly. Agriculture and mining throughput, taxation capacity and construction speed each #p +10%#!. This state separately applies Armed Forces approval #n −1#! and loyalty #n −1#! to serving generals and admirals; concurrent states stack. Costs #n 5#! public confidence per year.
english.nesnd_cne_camp_stop_tt: Stop this state’s monthly progress and remove its production, taxation and construction benefits and its associated military approval and officer loyalty penalties.
english.nesnd_cne_funding_requirements: Land reform remains active, the treasury can meet the cost, a year has passed since the previous grant, and no proposal awaits a reply.
english.nesnd_land_survey_outcome_tt: Propose industrial funding for the eligible state with the highest unemployment.
english.nesnd_land_military_outcome_tt: Propose relief for the eligible state with the highest unemployment among those facing starvation.
english.nesnd_cne_funding.1.d: The governor of [SCOPE.sState('nesnd_cne_funding_state').GetName] reports that many people leaving the estates lack the skills needed by workshops and struggle to find a living in town. The Ministry of Revenue proposes a grant for practical schools and workshop expansion. Learning a new trade would give these families the means to use the freedom promised by land reform.
english.nesnd_cne_funding.2.d: The governor of [SCOPE.sState('nesnd_cne_funding_state').GetName] requests additional relief. Families without an income are cutting their meals, and the towns offer too few jobs to support them. The Ministry of Revenue proposes a year of additional payments through the existing relief institutions and has submitted the grant for approval.

english.nesnd_reform_completion_tt: Reach #v 100#! reform progress, maintain sound livelihoods and institutions for #v 12#! consecutive months, and keep local disorder below #v 50#!. The monarchy must remain, confidence must endure, and no coup or revolutionary civil war may have occurred.
english.nesnd_reform_failure_tt: The reform fails if confidence runs out, monarchy ends, a revolution or secession war breaks out, or a coup succeeds. Extreme crisis also causes failure: at least fifteen months of reports, twelve consecutive distressed months, disorder of 90, national turmoil above 40%, legitimacy below 25, and war or a bankruptcy penalty.
english.ce_cne_land_reform_goal: Advance land commercialisation, urbanisation and military-estate reform, and consolidate the land revolution.

english.nesnd_cne_consolidation_rules:
#bold Consolidation#!
Schools level #v 2#!, literacy #v 48%#!, unemployment at most #v 6%#!, food insecurity at most #v 8%#!, living standards at least #v 11#! and market access at least #v 85%#!. Social Security level #v 2#! and living standards #v 12#! allow up to #v 12%#! unemployment. Non-negative bureaucracy, peace and no bankruptcy penalty are required.

#bold Local disorder#!
States with at least #v 500,000#! inhabitants interrupt consolidation after six months above #v 20%#! unemployment, #v 25%#! food insecurity or #v 10%#! severe starvation. National and local rates use workforce; subsistence workers are employed.

Complete at #v 100#! progress, #v 12#! consecutive qualifying months and disorder below #v 50#!. The rapid-reform reward requires completion within 48 months, at least 24 consecutive qualifying months and disorder below 30.
english.nesnd_jp_mining_reason: Collecting taxes and raising soldiers were once the duties of the warrior class. Mining and manufacturing require merchants as well. The mineral wealth of the north gives Edo new revenues, but also new partners: men without swords who are growing wealthy and expect the government to protect their businesses.
english.nesnd_jp_arsenals_reason: Arsenals and shipyards bring military spending into the towns. Contractors want dependable orders; officers resent having to bargain over the price of their equipment. As the workshops grow, these negotiations are becoming part of the business of government.
english.nesnd_jp_metal_cities_reason: The castle town grew around the lord’s fortress and the homes of his retainers. Now workers, apprentices and shopkeepers are settling in new streets, with children who need schooling. A town built to serve its lord is becoming a society with demands of its own.
english.nesnd_jp_cash_crops_reason: The ports bring the prices of distant markets into the countryside. Cotton, silk and tea have found new buyers, and both landowners and merchants want a larger share of the proceeds. The work of rural households is increasingly governed by decisions made far from their villages.
english.nesnd_jp_textiles_reason: Merchants who once bought cotton and silk from scattered households are bringing weavers together in larger mills. Wage work offers a new livelihood to people leaving the land, though it also subjects familiar skills to the discipline of a foreman. For the merchants, it promises closer control over production.
english.nesnd_jp_consumer_goods_reason: Food, furniture and household goods are finding customers beyond the wealthiest homes. Their manufacturers have acquired a reason to care about ordinary incomes. Families struggling to feed themselves have little to spend on other goods, limiting sales and putting pressure on prices and profits.
english.nesnd_jp_living_standards_reason: Families who have found work in the mills must still pay rent, buy food and find money for their children’s schooling. They have brought labour and tax revenue to the towns, and expect a share in their prosperity. The promise of a better life will be judged against these everyday expenses.
english.nesnd_jp_food_supply_reason: Harvests, fishing boats and grain merchants sustain life in the towns. When food prices rise, complaints from the markets soon reach the authorities. The government must keep food coming into the towns at prices their people can afford.
english.nesnd_jp_food_cities_reason: The grain trade brings customers, and craftsmen and apprentices settle near them. New neighbourhoods need schools; offices and booksellers need paper. Town institutions are taking on duties once left to village households and clans.
english.nesnd_jp_food_processing_reason: The towns need food that can be stored and carried over long distances. Grain and fish merchants want customers beyond the harvest season. Canning offers a way to combine purchasing, processing and transport in one business, while food factories could provide work after the harvest is over.
english.nesnd_jp_living_year: The living standard, school and urban development goals have been met for #v 12#! consecutive months
english.nesnd_jp_cohesion_reason: The domains of the shogunate, rural clans and merchants of the castle towns once upheld their own local orders. Schools and public administration connect distant communities, while flourishing commerce ties more livelihoods together. Security at home and the country’s fortunes in war shape confidence in a shared future.
english.nesnd_jp_cohesion_doubt: Public trust in the government is faltering, and local divisions are deepening.
english.nesnd_jp_cohesion_calm: The regions continue to uphold a common political order.
english.nesnd_jp_cohesion_confident: Confidence in a shared future encourages cultural assimilation.\nEach month, there is a #v 30%#! chance for people in one eligible owned [concept_state] to adopt [GetCulture('japanese').GetName] culture, up to #v 10%#! of that state's total population. Religion remains unchanged.
english.nesnd_jp_cohesion_confident_jiangnan: Confidence in a shared future encourages cultural assimilation.\nEach month, there is a #v 30%#! chance for people in one eligible owned [concept_state] to adopt [GetCulture('ce_wuu').GetName] culture, up to #v 10%#! of that state's total population. Religion remains unchanged.
english.nesnd_jp_politics_reason: After unifying Japan, the Toyotomi advanced into Korea with the Wu ruler's aid and secured their domains to the east. The authority of the Ming court, their own armies and Osaka's financial houses sustained the Taiko shogunate. New wealth and learning are changing these relationships. Merchants, officers and scholars seek a greater say in government. Disputes over appointments, the army and the law now concern who will control the state.
english.nesnd_jp_court_reform_reason: The old retainers want reform carried out in the monarch’s name. Merchants and officials trained in the new schools seek legal protection from arbitrary levies and local power. The crown can bring them together, but their respective rights remain to be settled.
english.nesnd_jp_military_reform_reason: The officers regard the army as the country’s most dependable institution. They seek common control over recruitment, training and supplies, bringing provincial forces under national direction. Arsenals and tool workshops would equip this army, while a concentrated government could carry the officers’ programme into the provinces.
english.nesnd_jp_representative_reform_reason: Scholars debate public affairs, merchants watch taxation, and local communities seek someone to speak for them. Advocates of representative government would bring these concerns into an elected assembly and subject those in power to open debate. Wider education can allow more people to understand the laws and take part in public life.
english.nesnd_jp_nation_reason: The promises made in pursuit of independence now confront the government. Who will pay for defence, who will set the tariffs, and how much authority will remain in local hands? Those who contributed money and those who served expect a place in the new state.
english.nesnd_jp_new_army_reason: Hereditary warriors and local loyalties sustained the old armies, with recruitment and training varying between domains. The country needs organized manpower, trained officers and forces that answer to a common command. Whether defence rests on a standing army or a national militia, military service must support the affairs of the nation.
english.nesnd_jp_open_diplomacy_reason: Tributary ties and maritime restrictions once placed diplomacy and trade within an overlord’s arrangements. We need to open our ports, send out merchant ships and negotiate with other countries in our own name. Lasting sovereignty will give these exchanges a government they can rely upon.
english.nesnd_jp_open_ports_reason: Japan’s overseas trade has long been confined to a few designated ports by strict prohibitions. Merchants seek distant raw materials and wider markets for their produce. The government must arrange the opening of the ports and confront those whose influence rests on the old restrictions.
english.nesnd_jp_islands_reason: Honshu has been reunited, but the question of Kyushu and Shikoku remains unsettled. Their ports and sea routes matter to trade and defence in southern Japan. The government may seek the remaining territories or accept the existing borders and relinquish its claims.
english.nesnd_jp_choose_court_desc: The dynasty can bring loyal retainers and reformers together. Preserve the crown, appoint capable officials, and give representative deliberation and enterprise a place in the state.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
english.nesnd_jp_choose_military_desc: The army needs a common command, and the state needs orders that can be carried through. Back the officers in reorganizing recruitment and supply, drawing provincial manpower and revenues into a common defence.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
english.nesnd_jp_choose_representative_desc: Public affairs concern everyone who pays taxes, serves or earns a living. Bring more representatives into government, subject officials to public debate, and let voters influence the conduct of the state.\n\nThe policy cannot be changed for #v 12#! months. Changing policy resets reform progress.
english.nesnd_jp_advance_reform_desc: Fund the advocates of reform so that their proposals can more quickly become law.
english.nesnd_jp_abandon_reform_desc: Withdraw the current programme and end the government’s reform campaign. Reform progress is lost, and reforms cannot be proposed again for #v 24#! months. Existing laws and buildings remain.
english.nesnd_jp_mercantile_ports_desc: Allow merchants to trade overseas, using tariffs to support state revenue and domestic commerce.
english.nesnd_jp_protected_ports_desc: Open the sea routes to obtain the materials our factories need, while using tariffs to support domestic producers in the wider market.
english.nesnd_jp_islands_settlement_desc: Relinquish our territorial claims to Kyushu and Shikoku and accept the current borders.
english.nesnd_jp_court_policy: Constitutional reform proceeds under the crown.
english.nesnd_jp_military_policy: Centralize authority and reorganize the army and its supplies.
english.nesnd_jp_representative_policy: Expand representation and protect public debate.
english.nesnd_jp_unsettled_policy: The government has yet to choose a course for reform.
english.nesnd_jp_nation_subject: The country is a subject again, with foreign affairs constrained by its overlord.
english.nesnd_jp_nation_independent: The country governs its own domestic and foreign affairs.
english.nesnd_jp_reform_settled: Reform progress is full and the chosen reforms have remained in force for #v 12#! months
english.nesnd_jp_nation_complete: Industrial, military and diplomatic development is complete, and the country has remained independent for #v 12#! consecutive months
english.nesnd_jp_independent_state: The Standing of an Independent State
english.nesnd_jp_development.1.d: Foreign envoys now deal directly with our government. Defence and overseas affairs, once conducted through an overlord, rest on institutions of our own.\n\nThe merchants and local leaders who supported independence have not retired from public life. They have brought new petitions, expecting the government to honour its promises.
english.nesnd_jp_development.1.a: We shall decide our own affairs.
english.nesnd_jp_development.2.d: New arrangements for appointing officials are in place, and the laws have changed how power is distributed. Families accustomed to holding local office by birth must now contend with positions and powers defined by the state. Officials, soldiers and merchants who took part in reform are finding their places within these arrangements, which now guide the conduct of public affairs.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign_reason: Aid from the mainland court helped the Toyotomi subdue Japan, binding tribute and maritime trade to the politics of the islands. Greater autonomy touches an overlord’s revenue, naval interests and influence in Japan. Those interests endure even when the old obligations are dissolved.
english.nesnd_jp_korea_reason: The mines and ports of southern Korea sustain trade across the strait. Local merchants depend on those routes, while provincial elites resist surrendering civil affairs to officials from across the sea. Arguments often come down to who will control the next levy.
english.nesnd_jp_envoy_away: Our envoy is awaiting a reply.
english.nesnd_jp_envoy_rest: The delegation is not yet ready to depart again. Envoys may be sent once every #v 6#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_subject_treaties: The country remains subject to an overlord and may negotiate over autonomy and development. Envoys may be sent once every #v 6#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_independent_treaties: The country may seek foreign assistance and union on its own behalf. Envoys may be sent once every #v 6#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_korea_across_the_strait: Territorial questions in Korea remain open to negotiation.
english.nesnd_jp_korea_governors_status: Governors direct taxation and civil administration in our Korean territories.
english.nesnd_jp_korea_councils_status: Local councils take part in civil administration and education.
english.nesnd_jp_korea_undecided: The government has yet to settle how its Korean territories will be administered.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_autonomy_desc: Ask the overlord to relax its control and raise our subject relationship by one autonomy level.\n\nAcceptance will establish a #v 5#!-year truce between the two countries.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_independence_desc: Ask the overlord to end the subject relationship and recognize our right to govern our own affairs.\n\nAcceptance will establish a #v 5#!-year truce between the two countries.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_reform_permission_desc: Seek the overlord’s assent to domestic reform, allowing us to reconsider appointments, military administration and political representation.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_union_permission_desc: Ask the overlord to permit negotiations with other Japanese subjects over a voluntary union.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_overlord_capital: Seek Development Funds from the Overlord
english.nesnd_jp_seek_overlord_capital_desc: Ask the overlord to fund workshops and the training of skilled workers, giving domestic production room to grow.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_capital_cne_desc: Seek development funds from the northern government, offering closer commercial ties as a reason to support our growing industries.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_capital_hus_desc: Approach Dongzhou for funds to build workshops, making the case for closer trade and industrial development.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
english.nesnd_jp_seek_capital_usm_desc: The southern government has long-standing commercial ties with Japan. Draw on these connections to seek funds for workshops and the training of skilled labour.\n\nAfter receiving assistance, further funding is unavailable for #v 3#! years.
english.nesnd_jp_independence_play_desc: Issue an ultimatum for independence, opening an independence [concept_diplomatic_play] and preparing to enforce the demand through war.
english.nesnd_jp_union_jap_desc: Propose a union to $JAP$. If accepted, their country will be annexed into ours and governed by our state.
english.nesnd_jp_union_jtk_desc: Propose a union to $JTK$. If accepted, their country will be annexed into ours and governed by our state.
english.nesnd_jp_union_jim_desc: Propose a union to $JIM$. If accepted, their country will be annexed into ours and governed by our state.
english.nesnd_jp_korean_governor_desc: Appoint governors to centralize taxation and civil administration in our Korean territories, giving the government closer control over local revenue and affairs.\n\nKorean policy cannot be changed again for #v 24#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_korean_councils_desc: Bring local councils into civil administration and education, seeking local cooperation to ease resistance to our rule.\n\nKorean policy cannot be changed again for #v 24#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_korean_envoy_desc: Offer a settlement to Korea or its overlord. If accepted, our holdings in Busan and Yangho will pass to Korea, and we will relinquish our claims to both regions.\n\nEnvoys may be sent once every #v 6#! months.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d1: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] seeks greater authority over its own affairs and asks us to relax the present subject relationship. The envoy argues that greater autonomy would let the local government respond to domestic needs while preserving ties between our countries.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d2: An envoy from [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] asks us to end the subject relationship. Their government seeks control over diplomacy, the military and trade, and wishes to deal with us as an independent country. We must decide whether to relinquish our authority as overlord.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d3: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] wishes to reform appointments, military administration and political representation. Its envoy seeks our assent so that the government can rally supporters and pursue its programme. The existing subject relationship would remain in place.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d4: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] is seeking funds for workshop construction. Its envoy asks us for a grant to expand production and train skilled workers, arguing that growing industry would deepen ties between our countries.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d5: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] proposes a settlement over southern Korea. Its government offers to relinquish claims to Busan and Yangho and transfer any territory it still holds there to Korea. The envoy asks us to accept these terms and settle the dispute.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d6: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] asks us to recognize its government as the leader of Japanese unification and place our territory under its rule. Accepting would end our existence as a separate state.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d7: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] seeks our permission to negotiate union with other Japanese subjects. Its government would lead the union, with each invited country surrendering its separate government only by consent. We must decide whether to allow such negotiations within the existing subject order.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.1.d: An envoy from [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_sender').GetNameNoFormatting] has arrived with a proposal concerning relations between our countries and awaits our reply.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.2.d: Our envoy has returned from [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting] with an agreement. Their government has accepted the proposal.
english.nesnd_jp_foreign.3.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting] has rejected the terms carried by our envoy. We failed to persuade them to concede, and the exchange has strained relations between our countries.
english.nesnd_jp_development.2.d_court: The court has settled new arrangements for representation and public office. The monarch still has the company of old retainers, but provincial administration is admitting officials with a different education.\n\nReformers loyal to the crown believe these concessions will preserve the monarchy. Whether those who have gained a voice will be satisfied remains an open question.
english.nesnd_jp_development.2.d_military: The officers have secured the centralized government they sought. Recruitment, training and supplies come under common direction, and local officials must carry out the government’s orders. Arsenals and tool workshops equip the expanded army, giving the military administration the means to enforce its policy in the provinces.
english.nesnd_jp_development.2.d_representative: Those entitled to vote now choose their representatives, and newspapers can debate the conduct of government. Officials face new rules of appointment, while political argument has spread beyond the old ruling families.\n\nSchools are bringing more people into this world. How the next generation will use these rights is theirs to decide.
english.nesnd_jp_sovereign_year: Has remained independent for #v 12#! consecutive months
english.nesnd_jp_establish_edo_reason: Edo now governs extensive northern territories. Garrisons can hold the roads, but they cannot conduct every part of provincial administration. The government needs officials to organise its revenue and spending, while the castle towns must accommodate merchants, craftsmen and people seeking work away from home. A country capable of sustaining ordinary government will be better placed to seek greater powers.
english.nesnd_jp_establish_kyoto_reason: The courtiers of Kyoto and the merchants of Osaka have different connections and interests. Courtly rank does not pay soldiers, and private wealth does not become public revenue of its own accord. Officials must organise taxation and administration in the territories they govern so that the towns can sustain the new government.
english.nesnd_jp_establish_toyotomi_reason: Partition has deprived the Toyotomi retainers of their former authority over Japan, but the troops and households remaining in the west still need support. Old prestige cannot settle who collects the revenue or conducts local government. A dependable administration must be established in the surviving territories, with castle towns serving as centres of government, taxation and employment.
english.nesnd_jp_establishment_required_tt: The country has established a functioning provincial administration.
english.nesnd_jp_independence_cooldown_tt: At least six months have passed since our last independence play.
english.nesnd_jp_union_permission_required_tt: Our overlord has authorised us to unite the Japanese states.
english.nesnd_jp_mercantile_ports_junior_desc: Replace seclusion with mercantilism and permit overseas commerce. The common market’s tariffs remain under the control of its leading country.
english.nesnd_jp_protected_ports_junior_desc: Adopt protectionist trade laws and open our ports. The common market’s tariffs remain under the control of its leading country.
english.nesnd_south_succession_board_reason: Whose realm is Southern Ming: the Zhu emperor’s, or the Zheng family’s creation? Nanjing retains the imperial succession, while the Southern Administration in Hangzhou commands the troops and revenues that sustain reform. The Western provinces and Hangzhou could postpone their dispute over sovereign and minister while resisting the North. With reform reaching deep into provincial life, they can no longer avoid the question of who will govern.\n\nHuguang’s academies and Xiangfan’s troops uphold the Zhu succession, while Sichuan’s republicans continue to debate the Southern Administration’s reforms. Governors in the Southern Seas and lords in Japan weigh the land, money and soldiers a new dynasty might demand. Representatives in the Assembly of Rites, ministers in the cabinet and provincial commanders will eventually have to answer for their choices.
english.nesnd_south_succession_board_status: The provinces and overseas states are declaring their positions and preparing their governments and forces. The dispute over Southern government now reaches across the seas.
english.nesnd_board_country_metrics:
Regular #v [Country.GetRegularBattalions|0]#! / Conscriptable #v [Country.CalcConscriptableBattalions|0]#!　Ships #v [Country.GetNumShips|0]#!
Fixed balance @money![Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_board_fixed_balance').GetValue|D+]　[concept_bureaucracy] [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_board_bureaucracy').GetValue|D+]
[concept_legitimacy] #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_board_legitimacy').GetValue|0]#!　Army projection #v [Country.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_board_army_projection').GetValue|1]#!
Supply preparations: [Country.GetCustom('nesnd_board_supply_loc')]
[Country.GetCustom('nesnd_south_ready_loc')]
english.nesnd_board_stance_available_tt: The civil war has not begun, and six months have passed since our last change of allegiance. Xiangfan remains committed to Ming; the central court cannot choose neutrality or autonomy.
english.nesnd_board_stance_effect_tt: Declare our alignment, fixed for #v 6 months#!. Withdrawing an existing commitment also cancels unfulfilled consent to integration or cession and reduces relations with the centre by #n 15#!.
english.nesnd_board_choose_ming_desc: The Zhu succession remains the recognised authority of the Southern provinces and overseas states. Support Ming government under the constitution and limits on Hangzhou’s dominance.
english.nesnd_board_choose_wu_desc: The Zheng family has long commanded the Southern realm’s military and fiscal power. Support the King of Wu in founding a dynasty whose constitution defines the powers of monarch and assembly.
english.nesnd_board_choose_neutral_desc: The Ming court and Hangzhou press rival claims. Remain outside the succession dispute for now and attend to our own trade and defence.
english.nesnd_board_choose_autonomy_desc: As the court disputes the succession, seek control of our own taxation, appointments and defence. Make our position clear to both Ming and Wu.
english.nesnd_board_not_ming_tt: This country has not declared support for the Ming court.
english.nesnd_board_not_wu_tt: This country has not declared support for the Zheng regime.
english.nesnd_board_not_neutral_tt: This country has not declared neutrality.
english.nesnd_board_not_autonomy_tt: This country has not declared its intention to seek autonomy.
english.nesnd_cne_arable_share_tt: In our Chinese heartland and northeastern states, developed farmland occupies at least #v 6%#! of arable land.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence_waning: Petitions multiply, and the court’s promises carry less weight.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence_rebellion: Republican armies have risen. Former comrades face one another in battle.
english.nesnd_cne_confidence_aftermath: The upheaval of the war has yet to subside.
english.nesnd_cne_employment_condition: Unemployment is no higher than 6%, or 12% with Social Security at least level 2 and Standard of Living at least 12.
english.nesnd_cne_livelihood_condition: No more than 8% of the workforce faces starvation; Standard of Living is at least 11 and Market Access at least 85%. No state is suffering a prolonged, severe livelihood crisis.
english.nesnd_cne_stability_condition: Living conditions and institutions have remained secure for twelve consecutive months.
english.nesnd_cne_civil_failure: A revolution or secession war has begun.
english.nesnd_cne_crisis_failure: Severe hardship has lasted a year, Local Disorder has reached 90, Turmoil exceeds 40%, and Legitimacy is below 25. The Empire is also at war or still suffering the effects of bankruptcy.
english.nesnd_ming_host_huguang_desc: Prefer Huguang if the court leaves the capital. Its government must support Ming and be able to act independently.
english.nesnd_ming_host_sichuan_desc: Prefer Sichuan if the court leaves the capital. Its government must support Ming and be able to act independently.
english.nesnd_ming_host_effect_tt: When the provinces break with the centre, establish the court in refuge here if possible; otherwise consider the other available host.
english.nesnd_ming_renew_convocation_desc: Summon representatives of the provinces and states to reconsider the positions of the Ming court and the King of Wu.
english.nesnd_ming_court.3.d: The accompanying ministers have reached the court’s refuge, and the local government is making room for them. Its army must still raise supplies and its administrative commissions govern the province; now it must also maintain the travelling court. Ming loyalism has acquired a centre to serve, and the host must bear the first costs of breaking with Hangzhou.\n\nEnvoys continue to arrive from the provinces and overseas states. Claims once debated in the Assembly of Rites and cabinet must now be sustained by military strength.
english.nesnd_ming_court.9.d: Neither Huguang nor Sichuan can presently receive the court, which must remain in Nanjing. Ming loyalists must continue seeking provincial support while negotiating with Hangzhou, which controls the troops and revenues. The Zheng claim to the throne is already before us; deliberations in the capital will determine how much room remains to act.
english.nesnd_ming_court.9.a: Negotiate in the capital and defer succession.
english.nesnd_ming_court.10.d: Opponents of the new dynasty have not formed a coalition capable of taking up arms. Appointments, taxation, military obligations and overseas status remain disputed. Hangzhou must keep answering those demands if Zheng rule is to win acceptance, while Ming loyalists continue seeking allies.
english.nesnd_ming_court_transfer_effect_tt: Take control of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName], with its existing forces, treasury, lands and tax system. If the legitimate Ming monarch accompanies the court, establish a monarchy under that ruler.
english.nesnd_ming_court.12.d: The provinces have broken with the centre, but circumstances have changed in the government chosen to receive the court. Unable to leave the capital, Ming loyalists must seek another host in Huguang or Sichuan capable of protecting the sovereign and maintaining the court. Every further day in Nanjing makes it harder to escape Hangzhou’s arrangements.
english.nesnd_ming_court.12.a: Remain in the capital and seek another opening.
english.nesnd_ming_court.12.b: Serve the new dynasty and abandon the evacuation.
english.nesnd_ming_seek_refuge_desc: Send envoys again to Huguang and Sichuan to find a government able to receive the court and uphold the Ming succession.
english.nesnd_ming_after_truce_reason: The truce has not returned the court to Nanjing. Ming loyalist provinces retain their armies and revenues, while Hangzhou has not abandoned its imperial claim. The court must rebuild its finances and seek allies before it can recover the old capital and settle the succession.
english.nesnd_ming_after_truce_status: In a new war, take Nanjing and the Wu capital and meet the terms for a restoration settlement.
english.nesnd_ming_refuge_available_tt: The succession confrontation or war is still underway. A Ming supporter in Huguang or Sichuan must be independent, hold its capital and be free of another player's control.
english.nesnd_qe1_agenda_status_econ: The reformers are gaining ground at court.
english.nesnd_qe1_agenda_status_army: The military faction is courting imperial favor.
english.nesnd_qe1_agenda_status_neutral: The court remains divided over the Empire's future.
english.nesnd_qe1_agenda_journal_reason: Since the Qin armies withdrew to Ili, the Chen imperial house has continued to look east toward the Jade Gate. Its soldiers and military nobility are less eager to march again. The Empire must restore production and tax revenue; the army needs recruits and pay. The reformers would begin with the laws that govern farmers, artisans and merchants. The military faction insists that imperial decrees will carry little weight in the provinces without an army to enforce them.
english.nesnd_qe1_economy_journal_reason: The reformers seek a free market in land, freedom for merchants to conduct their business, and a voice at court for men of property. Only by restoring its people's prosperity, they argue, can the Western Empire afford to challenge its eastern rivals again.
english.nesnd_qe1_army_journal_reason: The army has no wish to squander its strength on another hasty eastern expedition. Its leaders demand new regiments, a secure hold over Persia, and fresh lands and revenues on the Indian and Russian frontiers. Only then will they consider the country beyond the Jade Gate.
english.nesnd_qe1_econ_ready_status: The reformers' three laws are in force, and new workshops and railways strengthen their position.
english.nesnd_qe1_army_ready_status: The army has expanded, and victories on the western frontier have raised its standing.
english.nesnd_qe1_agenda_gate_tt: This proposal cannot be submitted again for six months.
english.nesnd_qe1_law_push_button_desc: Order officials to advance the legislation. Opposition from the military and landowners must no longer keep it from the court.
english.nesnd_qe1_economy_push_button_desc: Press the reform agenda at court, demanding concessions from the military and rural associations so that economic recovery and legal reform take priority.
english.nesnd_qe1_army_petition_button_desc: Send the new regimental rolls and reports of frontier victories to Ili, and demand recognition for the military faction's achievements.
english.nesnd_qe1_economy_petition_button_desc: The workshops, railways and new laws are bearing fruit. Petition the court to carry the reforms forward.
english.nesnd_qe1_angovernment_desc: The new commercial and industrial order strengthens the loyalty earned by rising living standards.
english.nesnd_qe1_stalled_desc: Years of indecision have made falling living standards a greater source of radicalism.
english.nesnd_qe1.1.a: Our people's prosperity must come first.
english.nesnd_qe1.1.d: The reformers have set the government’s course. Scholars and industrialists who supported reform have gained political influence, while the army and its supporters among the urban middle classes have lost ground. The new government looks to economic recovery and legal reform to win public support.
english.nesnd_qe1.2.a: Bring order to the army and the state.
english.nesnd_qe1.2.d: The military faction has won the government’s support and will take a greater part in recruitment, supply and appointments. Officials who argued for economic recovery and legal reform have failed to set its course. Ili has made expansion of the army a priority.
english.nesnd_qe1.3.a: We have squandered too many years.
english.nesnd_qe1.3.d: For ten years the court has argued over land, military pay and appointments without reaching a settlement. The provinces have heard promise after promise of imperial renewal. Fewer now believe that another decree will improve their lot.
english.nesnd_qe1_unity_hope: Farmers, townspeople and soldiers still see their future in the Empire.
english.nesnd_qe1_unity_doubt: Older local identities are reviving, and imperial authority is weakening in the provinces.
english.nesnd_qe1_unity_crisis: Old ethnic names have become rallying cries for armed resistance.
english.nesnd_qe1_unity_journal_reason: Trade routes, village communities and military colonies brought peoples of many origins under the Chen emperors of Qin. The Western Regions Han-Qiang emerged from that expansion and now provide much of the country’s manpower and revenue. Prosperity encourages a common identity. Conscription and hardship can lead people back to older loyalties of kinship, faith and homeland.
english.nesnd_qe1_uprising_journal_reason: Petitions no longer satisfy the associations of the frontier. They are gathering provisions, approaching old noble families and religious leaders, and challenging imperial tax collectors and recruiting officers in the name of local peoples. Ili may yet recover their allegiance. Delay will allow scattered resistance to grow into a common revolt.
english.nesnd_qe1_identity.1.a: The provinces have lost faith in our promises.
english.nesnd_qe1_identity.1.d: The villages and military colonies of [SCOPE.sStateRegion('nesnd_qe1_declining_region').GetName] are rediscovering their past. Old ethnic names, sacred texts and local ties are once again the foundations of trust. About half of the province's Western Regions Han-Qiang now identify as [SCOPE.sCulture('nesnd_qe1_return_culture').GetName] and follow the [SCOPE.sReligion('nesnd_qe1_return_religion').GetName] faith.
english.nesnd_qe1_court_status: The imperial house, provincial literati and army are competing for control of the government.
english.nesnd_qe1_court_journal_reason: The imperial house draws on the prestige of past conquests and the loyalty of officials who owe it their position. Provincial literati work through schools, trading houses and public offices; the army commands the force on which imperial expansion depends. Each faction needs the others to govern, yet each seeks authority over appointments, revenue and military command.
english.nesnd_qe1_patron_crown_button_desc: Give more offices to soldiers and administrators loyal to the imperial house.
english.nesnd_qe1_patron_literati_button_desc: Give schools, trading houses and civil officials a greater voice at court.
english.nesnd_qe1_patron_army_button_desc: Raise the political standing of the army and its supporters in the towns.
english.nesnd_qe1_patron_cancel_button_desc: End the court's special support for this faction.
english.nesnd_qe1_coup_army_button_desc: Reorganize the state around the army and occupational corporations, placing autocratic authority in corporate institutions.
english.nesnd_qe1_coup_literati_button_desc: Establish a presidential republic with an elected president and a parliament chosen by proportional representation.
english.nesnd_qe1_coup_crown_button_desc: Reorganize the government as a monarchy administered by trained technocrats, restoring the imperial house to power.
english.law_nesnd_qe1_proportional_representatio: Property determines eligibility to vote, while literacy increases a voter’s political influence. Political groups form parliament and government according to their support.
english.nesnd_qe1_recovery_journal_reason: The Chen imperial house has not forgotten the passes of Hexi or the fields of Guanzhong. By recovering the roads to the east and rebuilding its army and administration, the Empire could make these ancestral lands the foundation of a renewed struggle for China.
english.nesnd_qe1_recovery.1.a: Rebuild our armies on the ancestral lands.
english.nesnd_qe1_recovery.1.b: Carry the reforms into the provinces first.
english.nesnd_qe1_recovery.1.d: Qin forces once again control the roads through Hexi and Guanzhong. The court must decide how to use its victory: prepare fresh armies for the march east, or first establish new institutions, industries and a common identity throughout the recovered provinces.
english.nesnd_qe1_fracture.1.a: Let all troops loyal to the court stand ready.
english.nesnd_qe1_fracture.2.a: Only the last of our lands remain.
english.nesnd_qe1_fracture.1.d: Officials and officers excluded from the imperial councils have gathered an army. Calling themselves loyalists, they denounce the faction that holds Ili and demand a new settlement by force. The struggle at court has become an armed rebellion.
english.nesnd_qe1_fracture.2.d: Provincial governments have raised new flags. The old names of Bukhara, Khwarezm and the steppe appear once more in military orders and tax rolls. Local rulers no longer acknowledge Ili's authority over their people, land or revenue. Beyond the few provinces still held by the court, the Empire is giving way to rival states.
english.nesnd_per_future_status_choice: The court has yet to settle its relations with Ili.
english.nesnd_per_future_status_aid: The government has chosen to seek support from Ili for expansion to the west.
english.nesnd_per_future_status_covert: Our envoys are approaching Central Asian leaders opposed to Ili.
english.nesnd_per_future_journal: The Future of the Near-Western Empire
english.nesnd_per_future_journal_reason: The Tang-Persian court knows both the military government of Qin and the merchants and great families of Persia. The Near-Western War brought land and prestige, but left the Empire's future course unsettled. The court may seek Ili's help for expansion to the west, or exploit unrest in Western Qin to pursue conquests of its own.
english.nesnd_per_civil_journal_reason: The offices introduced by the military government stand alongside local academies, religious schools and family networks. To make officials of these different backgrounds work together, the court needs reliable appointments and schools capable of training their successors.
english.nesnd_per_economy_journal_reason: Cotton fields, weavers and travelling merchants sustain Persia's prosperity. By linking the countryside to its towns with railways, the court hopes to make the lands won in the Near-Western War support new workshops as well as the army.
english.nesnd_per_west_journal_reason: The court has turned its attention beyond Mesopotamia. Qin military traditions and Persian wealth will sustain a new campaign of expansion. The Ottomans, Egypt and the states of Arabia may seek powerful allies of their own.
english.nesnd_per_east_journal_reason: Ili's authority is under challenge. The court intends to pursue its own interests along the routes through Central Asia and India. The frontiers of its former overlord now attract the attention of Persian commanders.
english.nesnd_per_seek_aid_button_desc: Request Qin assistance in reforming our administration and army, in preparation for expansion to the west.
english.nesnd_per_subvert_button: Approach the Peoples of Western Qin
english.nesnd_per_subvert_button_desc: Cultivate local leaders opposed to Ili and prepare to cast off our overlord's rule and expand eastward.
english.nesnd_per_civil_commit_button_desc: Appoint trained officials and bring the academies into closer cooperation with the administration.
english.nesnd_per_economy_commit_button_desc: Support our cotton fields, textile mills and railways, joining trade routes to industrial production.
english.nesnd_per_claim_levant_button: Assert Our Claims in the Levant
english.nesnd_per_claim_levant_button_desc: Present our territorial claims by diplomatic note. Powers with interests in the region may oppose them.
english.nesnd_per_claim_egypt_button: Assert Our Claims on the Nile
english.nesnd_per_claim_egypt_button_desc: Present our territorial claims by diplomatic note. Powers with interests in the region may oppose them.
english.nesnd_per_claim_arabia_button_desc: Present our territorial claims by diplomatic note. Powers with interests in the region may oppose them.
english.nesnd_per_claim_central_asia_button: Assert Our Claims in Central Asia
english.nesnd_per_claim_central_asia_button_desc: Present our territorial claims by diplomatic note. Powers with interests in the region may oppose them.
english.nesnd_per_claim_india_button_desc: Present our territorial claims by diplomatic note. Powers with interests in the region may oppose them.
english.nesnd_per.1.d: The officials sent by Qin bring experience beyond military administration. Working with local clerks, they are putting the laws in order so that officials, merchants and landowners need no longer contend with several conflicting sets of rules for the same business.
english.nesnd_per.2.d: The craftsmen who accompanied the mission have arrived in our workshops. They are teaching surveying, construction and machine maintenance. Local workers and merchants must now turn those skills into lasting enterprises.
english.nesnd_per.3.d: The Qin envoy has affirmed his court's support for our government. Officers and merchants with ties to Ili are reassured, and the endorsement has quieted the court's opponents for the time being.
english.nesnd_per.4.d: Our tributary relationship with Ili is settled, and the government has chosen expansion to the west. Commanders are preparing new campaigns, while merchants seek markets along the routes the army will take.
english.nesnd_per.5.a: The Near-Western War enters a new chapter.
english.nesnd_per.5.d: Our preparations among the local powers of Western Qin are complete. The court will pursue its own ambitions in Central Asia and India, free of orders from Ili.
english.nesnd_per.6.a: Deliver the note to the foreign courts.
english.nesnd_per.6.d: The court has formally asserted its claim to [SCOPE.sStateRegion('nesnd_per_claim_region').GetName]. Commanders and merchants can prepare their next moves. Possession of the territory must still be secured through diplomacy or war.
english.nesnd_per.7.d: A foreign power has opposed our claim to [SCOPE.sStateRegion('nesnd_per_claim_region').GetName]. The court has failed to secure recognition. It must improve its diplomatic position before renewing the demand.
english.nesnd_qe1_conversion_cohort_standard_of_: Western Regions Han-Qiang Standard of Living
Western Regions Han-Qiang Standard of Living
english.dp_nesnd_qe1_civil_desc: Rival factions take up arms for control of Qin.
english.dp_nesnd_qe1_civil_tooltip: Rival factions take up arms for control of Qin.
english.dp_nesnd_qe1_frontier_desc: The frontier states go to war against Ili.
english.dp_nesnd_qe1_frontier_tooltip: The frontier states go to war against Ili.
